# Matchalize — Full Codebase Dump

> Verbatim contents of all project source and configuration files.
> Generated 2026-10-18 20:29.
> Identical content to dumps/ -- kept as one file for grep and for tools without an attachment limit.
> Matchalize is an INTRA + INTER college network for all the colleges of India: users connect within their own campus (intra) AND across campuses (inter). Every user signs in via their own college academic email system (`.ac.in`), making each campus a private, verified community.

> **This file is not paste-safe.** At this size a chat UI truncates the
> paste silently and the reader cannot tell what it lost. To share this
> codebase, paste `dumps/00-INDEX.md` and only the chunks you need.

## Section — Root & Project Config

### ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

```
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Cancel superseded runs on the same ref — avoids burning minutes re-linting a
# branch that's already been superseded by a newer push.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: |
            package-lock.json
            client/package-lock.json
            server/package-lock.json

      # Root package-lock.json exists for the @playwright/test devDependency, so
      # `npm ci` runs at the root too — otherwise the lockfile check fails.
      - run: npm ci

      - run: npm ci --prefix client
      - run: npm ci --prefix server

      # Lint both sides. The server had no linter until now, so a large batch of
      # warnings is expected on the first run — oxlint exits 0 for warnings and
      # non-zero only for errors, which is the intended gate.
      - name: Lint client
        run: npm run lint --prefix client
      - name: Lint server
        run: npm run lint --prefix server

      # Build fails on a broken import/JSX syntax error, which the linter alone
      # won't catch.
      - name: Build client
        run: npm run build --prefix client

      # Pure-logic unit tests, no database or browser required. Both suites use
      # the built-in node:test runner, so this adds no dependency.
      #
      # Roulette's camera teardown is deliberately covered here rather than left
      # to end-of-project device testing: a leaked camera is invisible to a
      # reviewer but is the failure that reaches users, and the guarantee lives
      # in `stopStream`, which is testable without hardware.
      - name: Test server
        run: npm test --prefix server
      - name: Test client
        run: npm test --prefix client

      # dumps/ is committed and gets handed to other tools, so it must not
      # silently go stale: a stale dump means a reader gets code that no longer
      # matches the repo, and nothing in the dump tells them. --check re-parses
      # every chunk and diffs each embedded file against disk, so any edit that
      # isn't followed by `bash scripts/generate-dump.sh` fails here instead.
      - name: Verify dumps are current
        run: python3 regenerate_dumps.py --check

      - name: Syntax-check server entrypoints
        # `node --check` on the boot path — the routes are ESM with top-level
        # await, so this is the cheapest server-side smoke test without a
        # database. Mongoose models can't be checked this way, hence the boot
        # happens in the QA job below rather than here.
        run: |
          cd server
          for f in index.js config/db.js config/roulette.js models/index.js \
                   utils/age.js routes/messages.js routes/users.js \
                   routes/discover.js routes/alignments.js \
                   routes/notifications.js; do
            node --check "$f"
          done

  # Not wired up yet, deliberately. The QA harness (npm run qa) drives a real
  # browser against a real server and needs a live MongoDB, so it needs a
  # service container and a slower runner. Enable it once the harness is green
  # rather than adding a permanently failing job to every push.
  #
  # qa:
  #   runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  #   services:
  #     mongodb:
  #       image: mongo:7
  #       ports: ['27017:27017']
  #       options: >-
  #         --health-cmd "mongosh --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1})'"
  #         --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5
  #   steps:
  #     - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  #     - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  #       with: { node-version: 20 }
  #     - run: npm ci && npm ci --prefix client && npm ci --prefix server
  #     - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
  #     - run: npm run qa
```

### ./client/index.html

```
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover" />
    <!-- Initial chrome colour, replaced per-screen at runtime by utils/chrome.js.
         Defaults to the Deck's night desk so there is no white flash on first paint. -->
    <meta name="theme-color" content="#131313" />
    <!-- black-translucent (not "default"): this is what lets the page's own
         background paint UNDER the iOS status bar. With "default" iOS draws an
         opaque bar and the top edge can never match the screen below it, which
         is the seam this whole mechanism exists to hide. -->
    <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style" content="black-translucent" />
    <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icons/icon-192.png" />
    <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.json" />
    
    <!-- Neo-Brutalist Type System: Archivo Black (display) · Inter (body) · Space Mono (labels) · Caveat (hand).
         Playfair/Special Elite/Dancing Script remain only until the last sunlit screens are converted. -->
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
    <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Archivo+Black&family=Caveat:wght@700&family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=Space+Mono:wght@400;700&family=Playfair+Display:ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400&family=Special+Elite&family=Dancing+Script:wght@700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Material+Symbols+Outlined:opsz,wght,FILL,GRAD@20..48,100..700,0..1,-50..200&display=block" />
    
    <title>Matchalize — Your Campus. Your Story.</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="root"></div>
    <script type="module" src="/src/main.jsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>

### ./client/public/sw.js

```
// v2 → v3: the v2 cache had no eviction and was caching /uploads/ (photos),
// which are cookie-gated but served from cache without a server
// request. Bumping the name makes `activate` delete the whole old cache on the
// next load, purging what was already stored on real devices.
// Bump this every time caching behaviour changes — it is the only eviction
// mechanism here.
const CACHE_NAME = 'matchalize-v3';

const STATIC_ASSETS = [
  '/',
  '/index.html',
  '/manifest.json',
  '/icons/icon-192.png',
  '/icons/icon-512.png',
  '/icons/badge-72.png',
];

self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => cache.addAll(STATIC_ASSETS))
  );
  self.skipWaiting();
});

self.addEventListener('activate', (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    caches.keys().then((keys) =>
      Promise.all(keys.filter((k) => k !== CACHE_NAME).map((k) => caches.delete(k)))
    )
  );
  self.clients.claim();
});

// ─── FETCH HANDLER (was missing — cache was dead code) ───
// Network-first for navigation requests (always get fresh HTML)
// Cache-first for static assets (icons, manifest)
self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
  const { request } = event;
  const url = new URL(request.url);

  // Skip cross-origin requests (API calls to backend, Cloudinary, etc.)
  if (url.origin !== self.location.origin) return;
  // NEVER cache API responses — otherwise stale chat/notification data could be served
  if (url.pathname.startsWith('/api/')) return;
  // NEVER cache /uploads/ — these are the user's own photos.
  //
  // Two reasons, and the second is the serious one:
  //   1. They are unbounded user media. The cache below is cache-first with no
  //      eviction and no TTL, so every uploaded photo accumulated in the
  //      browser permanently — the cache only clears when someone hand-edits
  //      CACHE_NAME (see `activate`).
  //   2. `/uploads` is served behind `protect` (server/index.js). A cache hit is
  //      returned WITHOUT any request to the server, so no cookie is ever
  //      checked. On a shared device the next person to open the app would be
  //      served the previous user's photos straight out of the
  //      cache.
  //
  // In production uploads are Cloudinary URLs (cross-origin, already skipped by
  // the origin check above), so this only bit the local-disk fallback — but the
  // fallback is exactly what a staging/preview deploy uses, and the leak is real
  // there.
  if (url.pathname.startsWith('/uploads/')) return;
  // Skip non-GET requests
  if (request.method !== 'GET') return;

  // Network-first for navigation (HTML pages)
  if (request.mode === 'navigate') {
    event.respondWith(
      fetch(request)
        .then((response) => {
          const responseClone = response.clone();
          caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
            cache.put(request, responseClone);
          });
          return response;
        })
        .catch(() => {
          return caches.match('/index.html'); // Offline fallback
        })
    );
    return;
  }

  // Cache-first for static assets
  event.respondWith(
    caches.match(request).then((cached) => {
      if (cached) return cached;

      return fetch(request).then((response) => {
        if (!response || response.status !== 200) return response;

        const responseClone = response.clone();
        caches.open(CACHE_NAME).then((cache) => {
          cache.put(request, responseClone);
        });
        return response;
      });
    })
  );
});

self.addEventListener('push', (event) => {
  let data = { title: 'Matchalize', body: 'You have a new notification' };

  if (event.data) {
    try {
      data = event.data.json();
    } catch {
      data.body = event.data.text();
    }
  }

  const options = {
    body: data.body,
    icon: data.icon || '/icons/icon-192.png',
    badge: data.badge || '/icons/badge-72.png',
    vibrate: data.vibrate || [100, 50, 100],
    data: data.data || {},
    tag: data.data?.type || 'notification',
    renotify: true,
  };

  event.waitUntil(
    self.clients.matchAll({ type: 'window', includeUncontrolled: true }).then((clients) => {
      const hasVisibleClient = clients.some((c) => c.visibilityState === 'visible' && c.focused);
      if (hasVisibleClient) return;
      return self.registration.showNotification(data.title, options);
    })
  );
});

self.addEventListener('notificationclick', (event) => {
  event.notification.close();

  const data = event.notification.data;

  event.waitUntil(
    /* ⚠️ THIS CALLBACK MUST BE `async`. It uses `await client.focus()` below,
       and in a plain `.then()` callback `await` is a SyntaxError — which
       invalidates the ENTIRE file at parse time.

       That is not a cosmetic failure. A service worker that fails to parse is
       never registered at all, so `navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js')`
       rejected with `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'client'` and the whole
       app silently lost push notifications and offline support. The error
       surfaced only in the console as two unrelated-looking lines, which is why
       it went unnoticed.

       `matchAll` returns a promise; chaining `.then(async …)` is what makes the
       `await` legal inside it. */
    self.clients.matchAll({ type: 'window', includeUncontrolled: true }).then(async (clients) => {
      // `/?chat=<id>`, NOT `/chat/<id>`: the app has no router, so a path-based
      // URL would just boot to the deck and the tap would look broken.
      // AppShell reads this param and opens the conversation.
      const target = data.alignmentId ? `/?chat=${data.alignmentId}` : '/';
      for (const client of clients) {
        if (client.url.includes(self.location.origin) && 'focus' in client) {
          await client.focus();
          // Push the param onto the open tab rather than navigating, so the
          // already-mounted AppShell can act on it without a full reload.
          client.postMessage({ type: 'open-chat', alignmentId: data.alignmentId || null });
          return;
        }
      }
      return self.clients.openWindow(target);
    })
  );
});

## Section — Shared Contracts

### ./client/src/utils/ladder.js

```
/**
 * 🪜 PROFILE LADDER — client reader
 *
 * ⚠️ THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO `computeScore` IN THIS FILE.
 *
 * The score itself lives on the server (utils/ladder.js) and is stored as
 * `User.profileScore`. This module only reads the thresholds, which the server
 * ships through GET /config, so the profile bar, the gate, and any future nudge
 * all mark up against the same numbers instead of each hardcoding 45/75/100.
 *
 * Do not add a client-side scorer. The ladder gates the discover deck, so a
 * score the client could recompute is a score someone can edit in devtools and
 * use to walk straight through the gate. Render what the server sent.
 */

/**
 * Fallback used only if /config has not resolved (or failed). These MUST stay
 * equal to LADDER in server/utils/ladder.js — they are the last-resort values,
 * not an independent definition.
 */
export const LADDER_FALLBACK = {
  publish: 45,
  interact: 75,
  aspirational: 100,
};

/** Max photos a profile may hold. Mirrored by `slice(0, 4)` server-side. */
export const MAX_PHOTOS = 4;

/**
 * Read the thresholds off the /config payload.
 *
 * @param {object|null} config the AppConfigContext value
 * @returns {{publish:number, interact:number, aspirational:number}}
 */
export const readLadder = (config) => {
  const fromServer = config?.ladder;
  return {
    publish: fromServer?.publish ?? LADDER_FALLBACK.publish,
    interact: fromServer?.interact ?? LADDER_FALLBACK.interact,
    aspirational: fromServer?.aspirational ?? LADDER_FALLBACK.aspirational,
  };
};

/**
 * Which band a score falls in. Mirrors `bandFor` in server/utils/ladder.js —
 * the vocabulary is defined once per side, but both must agree.
 *
 * @param {number} score
 * @param {object} config
 * @returns {'locked'|'published'|'interactable'|'aspirational'}
 */
export const bandFor = (score, config) => {
  const { publish, interact, aspirational } = readLadder(config);
  const n = Number.isFinite(score) ? score : 0;
  if (n >= aspirational) return 'aspirational';
  if (n >= interact) return 'interactable';
  if (n >= publish) return 'published';
  return 'locked';
};

/**
 * True when the discover deck's interactive actions should be available.
 * Reads-only surfaces (your own profile, Letters, Roulette, received chats)
 * are NOT gated on this — see the deck-wide gate design.
 */
export const canInteract = (score, config) => {
  const band = bandFor(score, config);
  return band === 'interactable' || band === 'aspirational';
};

/**
 * Coerce whatever the API sent into a usable number. A user document predating
 * the field has no `profileScore` at all, so it arrives undefined and would
 * otherwise render as `NaN%` in the bar.
 */
export const readScore = (user) => {
  const n = Number(user?.profileScore);
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.max(0, Math.min(100, n)) : 0;
};
```

### ./server/routes/config.js

```
import express from 'express';
import Setting from '../models/Setting.js';
import {
  PROMPT_BANK, BRANCHES, YEARS, GENDERS, INTENTS, INTEREST_TAGS,
  PRONOUNS_OPTIONS, INTEREST_ICONS, INTEREST_ICON_FALLBACKS, APP_CONSTANTS,
} from '../config/appData.js';
import { LADDER } from '../utils/ladder.js';
import { collegeGateFilter } from '../utils/campusGate.js';
import College from '../models/College.js';

const router = express.Router();

// ─── IN-MEMORY TTL CACHE ───
// Config changes rarely, but this endpoint is hit on EVERY app load.
// Cache for 30s so simultaneous launches produce ONE DB query, not one per user.
const CACHE_TTL_MS = 30 * 1000;
let configCache = null;
let cacheExpiresAt = 0;

router.get('/', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    // 🏫 COLLEGES ARE ALWAYS FETCHED FRESH — deliberately outside the cache.
    //
    // This must happen before the cache short-circuit below. An operator who
    // just added a campus and then saw it missing from their own picker would
    // reasonably assume the Add button is broken. One small indexed query on a
    // handful of college rows is not worth a stale picker.
    //
    // Only ACTIVE colleges: deactivating one removes it from signup immediately,
    // while students who already verified through it are untouched.
    //
    // AND only gated-in ones. A campus outside ALLOWED_COLLEGES cannot sign up
    // (routes/auth.js resolveCollege refuses it), so listing it here would show
    // a student a selectable option that is guaranteed to fail at the email
    // step — the worst place to discover a closed door.
    const colleges = await College.find({ active: true, ...collegeGateFilter() }).sort({ name: 1 }).lean();
    const collegeList = colleges.map((c) => ({
      code: c.code,
      name: c.name,
      // Public campus information — it has to be exposed for the pre-filled
      // email suffix to work. It contains no student data whatsoever.
      domains: c.domains,
      city: c.city,
      state: c.state,
      country: c.country,
    }));

    // Serve the static remainder from cache if fresh
    if (configCache && Date.now() < cacheExpiresAt) {
      res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=30');
      return res.json({ ...configCache, colleges: collegeList });
    }

    // Check database for dynamic settings first
    const dbSetting = await Setting.findOne({ key: 'appConfig' });
    let payload;
    if (dbSetting) {
      payload = dbSetting.value;
    } else {
      // Fallback to static file if DB is empty
      payload = {
        prompts: PROMPT_BANK,
        branches: BRANCHES,
        years: YEARS,
        genders: GENDERS,
        intents: INTENTS,
        interests: INTEREST_TAGS,
        pronouns: PRONOUNS_OPTIONS,
        interestIcons: INTEREST_ICONS,
        interestIconFallbacks: INTEREST_ICON_FALLBACKS,
        // `colleges` is attached from the DB after this object is built — it is
        // no longer sourced from COLLEGE_MAP in appData.js. That constant
        // survives only as the seed in scripts/reset-colleges.mjs.
        constants: APP_CONSTANTS,
        splash: {
          videoUrl: process.env.SPLASH_VIDEO_URL || '/lover.mp4',
          tagline: process.env.SPLASH_TAGLINE || 'Your Campus. Your Story.',
        },
      };
    }

    // The ladder is attached AFTER the source is resolved, never inside either
    // branch. A stored `appConfig` document in the DB is an admin-authored
    // snapshot taken before the ladder existed, so if this were set in the
    // static fallback only, the thresholds would silently vanish from the
    // client the moment anyone saved that setting — and the gate would then
    // hardcode its own numbers instead of reading LADDER.interact.
    payload = { ...payload, ladder: LADDER };

    // Colleges were already fetched above, outside the cache. Attached here so
    // both the cached and uncached response paths carry the same fresh list.
    payload = { ...payload, ladder: LADDER, colleges: collegeList };

    configCache = payload;
    cacheExpiresAt = Date.now() + CACHE_TTL_MS;
    res.set('Cache-Control', 'public, max-age=30');
    res.json(payload);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Config route error:', error);
    res.status(500).json({ message: 'Server error fetching config' });
  }
});

export default router;
```

### ./server/utils/age.js

```
/**
 * 🎂 AGE IS DERIVED, NEVER STORED-TRUSTED
 *
 * `User.age` is written once during onboarding and never touched again, so it
 * silently drifts: a user who signs up at 18 in August is still 18 the
 * following October. Before this module, that stale number was rendered on the
 * Matches page and the chat header (alignments.js projected `age` straight out
 * of the database) while the Discover deck didn't show age at all.
 *
 * Every public surface now derives age from `dob` at read time instead, so a
 * card can never show a number that's out of date. `User.age` is still written
 * at onboarding for the few paths that can't compute on read (a Mongoose
 * `.populate()` in routes/notifications.js, and the two full-document profile
 * endpoints) — run `scripts/backfill-age.mjs` after deploying to refresh those.
 *
 * ⚠️ DOB IS NOT SENT TO CLIENTS. It is PII and is far more identifying than an
 * age, so withFreshAge() always strips it from the object it returns. That is
 * why surfaces read `dob` in their query but never pass it on.
 */

/**
 * Whole years elapsed since `dob`, calendar-aware — so someone whose birthday
 * is today is already their new age, and someone whose birthday was yesterday
 * is not off by one.
 *
 * @param {Date|string|number} dob
 * @param {Date} [now] injectable for tests
 * @returns {number|null} age, or null if `dob` is missing/unparseable
 */
export const computeAgeFromDob = (dob, now = new Date()) => {
  if (!dob) return null;
  const d = dob instanceof Date ? dob : new Date(dob);
  if (Number.isNaN(d.getTime())) return null;

  let age = now.getFullYear() - d.getFullYear();
  const monthDelta = now.getMonth() - d.getMonth();
  if (monthDelta < 0 || (monthDelta === 0 && now.getDate() < d.getDate())) {
    age -= 1;
  }
  return age;
};

/**
 * Attach a freshly-computed `age` to a plain object (a `.lean()` result or an
 * aggregation result) and remove `dob` from it.
 *
 * Deliberately returns a NEW object rather than mutating: the aggregation
 * results in routes/alignments.js are plain objects, but `.lean()` documents
 * elsewhere should stay untouched if the caller reuses them.
 *
 * Any pre-existing `age` key is overwritten — the whole point is that the
 * stored value may be stale.
 *
 * ⚠️ FALLBACK: if the document has no usable `dob`, the stored `age` is kept
 * rather than nulled. Onboarding requires `dob`, so a real user always has one;
 * the fallback exists for seeded/demo/QA rows (tests/society/personas.mjs
 * historically set `age` only) and any legacy
 * document predating the dob field. Without it those profiles would render as
 * "—" everywhere — worse than a stale number.
 */
export const withFreshAge = (user) => {
  if (!user) return user;
  const { dob, ...rest } = user;
  const computed = computeAgeFromDob(dob);
  return { ...rest, age: computed ?? rest.age ?? null };
};

### ./server/utils/collegeDomain.js

```
/**
 * 🔒 COLLEGE DOMAIN MATCHING — the whole verification boundary.
 *
 * An email is "college X's address" only when the domain after the @ is either
 * EXACTLY one of X's registered domains, or a subdomain of one (separated by a
 * real dot, so every IIT Bombay department address works from a single entry).
 *
 * ⚠️ WHY THIS FILE IS DELICATE
 *
 * A naive `endsWith` check accepts `attacker@iitb.ac.in.evil.com`, because
 * that string DOES end with "iitb.ac.in". The attacker owns `evil.com`, catches
 * the OTP, and is now a verified student. The dot-boundary requirement in
 * `domainMatches` is the only thing standing between that and a breach.
 *
 * Previously this lived as string-slicing in routes/auth.js — "take the label
 * immediately before .ac.in" — which was both wrong for any non-.ac.in domain
 * and forgeable. It is gone.
 */

/**
 * Strip an email down to its bare domain, or null if it isn't parseable.
 *
 * Deliberately strict: exactly one "@", something either side, no spaces. A
 * loose parser here is a security hole.
 *
 * @param {string} email
 * @returns {string|null} lowercased domain without a leading @
 */
export function extractDomain(email) {
  if (typeof email !== 'string') return null;
  const trimmed = email.trim().toLowerCase();
  const parts = trimmed.split('@');
  if (parts.length !== 2) return null;

  const [local, domain] = parts;
  if (!local || !domain) return null;
  if (/\s/.test(trimmed)) return null;
  // A domain needs at least one dot and no empty labels. Rejects "a@b" and
  // "x@iitb.ac.in@" style inputs that a lenient parser would wave through.
  if (!domain.includes('.')) return null;
  if (domain.startsWith('.') || domain.endsWith('.') || domain.includes('..')) return null;
  if (!/^[a-z0-9.-]+$/.test(domain)) return null;

  return domain;
}

/**
 * Does `domain` belong to `approved`?
 *
 * Exact match, or a subdomain of it. "Subdomain" means the remainder sits
 * behind a dot, which is the entire security property:
 *
 *   iitb.ac.in              === iitb.ac.in              → true
 *   cse.iitb.ac.in          endsWith .iitb.ac.in       → true
 *   notiitb.ac.in           endsWith .iitb.ac.in? NO   → false
 *   iitb.ac.in.evil.com     endsWith .iitb.ac.in? NO   → false
 *
 * @param {string} domain   already extracted, lowercased
 * @param {string} approved registered domain, lowercased, no @
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function domainMatches(domain, approved) {
  if (!domain || !approved) return false;
  const d = domain.toLowerCase();
  const a = approved.toLowerCase().replace(/^@/, '').trim();
  if (!a) return false;
  if (d === a) return true;
  return d.endsWith(`.${a}`);
}

/**
 * Full check: does this email address match ANY of these approved domains?
 *
 * @param {string} email
 * @param {string[]} approvedDomains
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export function emailMatchesCollege(email, approvedDomains) {
  const domain = extractDomain(email);
  if (!domain || !Array.isArray(approvedDomains) || approvedDomains.length === 0) return false;
  return approvedDomains.some((d) => domainMatches(domain, d));
}

/**
 * The best (longest) matching domain, for storing a sensible `collegeCode`
 * hint on an OTP record. Longest wins so `cse.iitb.ac.in` beats `iitb.ac.in`
 * when a college registers both.
 *
 * @param {string} email
 * @param {string[]} approvedDomains
 * @returns {string|null}
 */
export function matchDomain(email, approvedDomains) {
  const domain = extractDomain(email);
  if (!domain || !Array.isArray(approvedDomains)) return null;
  const hits = approvedDomains
    .map((a) => ({ a: a.toLowerCase().replace(/^@/, '').trim(), ok: domainMatches(domain, a) }))
    .filter((x) => x.ok)
    .sort((x, y) => y.a.length - x.a.length);
  return hits.length ? hits[0].a : null;
}

/**
 * Normalise a domain for storage: lowercase, no @, no leading/trailing dot.
 * Returns null for anything that can't be a domain, so callers can reject it.
 *
 * @param {string} raw
 * @returns {string|null}
 */
export function normaliseDomain(raw) {
  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null;
  const d = raw.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/^@/, '').replace(/^\.+|\.+$/g, '');
  if (!d || !d.includes('.') || /[^a-z0-9.-]/.test(d) || d.includes('..')) return null;
  return d;
}

### ./server/utils/geo.js

```
/**
 * 📍 DISTANCE — coarse bands, computed from stored coordinates.
 *
 * ── WHY BANDING AT ALL, AND WHY NOT EXACT KILOMETRES ──────────────────────
 * The deck shows people you could plausibly actually meet. A band answers that
 * question well enough ("Near you", "In your area") without publishing a
 * distance figure that narrows someone down. Publishing "14km away" on a card
 * is a materially different privacy act from publishing "In your area", and the
 * product gets nothing from the precision: nobody changes their behaviour
 * because the number is 14 instead of 19.
 *
 * ── WHY UNKNOWN IS NOT ZERO ───────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Every function here treats "we do not know where this person is" as its own
 * answer, never as "they are nearby". Collapsing unknown into 0 km would rank
 * a profile with no location as maximally close and float it to the top of the
 * deck — the exact class of bug `UNKNOWN_ACTIVITY_SCORE = 0.5` exists to
 * prevent on the activity side. `bandFor(null)` returns null, and callers sort
 * null LAST.
 *
 * ── WHY THE COORDINATES THEMSELVES ARE STORED ROUNDED ─────────────────────
 * `User.currentLatLng` is rounded to 2 decimal places before it is ever
 * persisted (see routes/users.js). That is a ~1.1km grid square. It is ample for
 * a 30km band and it means a home address cannot be reconstructed from the
 * database even if it were read. The rounding is a server-side control on
 * purpose: doing it client-side would leave the precise value in the request
 * body, the access logs, and anywhere else the request is captured.
 *
 * ── NO REVERSE GEOCODING, NO API KEY, NO COST ─────────────────────────────
 * Distance here is haversine between two stored points. Turning coordinates
 * into a city name would need a paid geocoding provider; nothing in this file
 * needs one, because the card label is derived from DISTANCE rather than from a
 * place name.
 */

const EARTH_RADIUS_KM = 6371;
const DEG_TO_RAD = Math.PI / 180;

/**
 * How long a stored location is still trusted before it stops affecting
 * ranking.
 *
 * 30 days, not 7. A student who sets their location in May and returns in July
 * must not silently drop out of distance ranking for two months over a long
 * break — that is the exact failure that made campus-only location untenable in
 * the first place. Beyond the window the reading is treated as unknown, which
 * is neutral, rather than kept indefinitely and quietly wrong.
 */
export const LOCATION_TTL_DAYS = 30;

/**
 * How far someone has to move before the stored position is treated as wrong
 * rather than merely imprecise.
 *
 * Without this, someone who travelled from Mumbai to Bangalore keeps being shown
 * as "Near you" to Mumbai profiles until the 30-day TTL finally expires — up to a
 * month of confidently wrong results. With it, the app corrects itself the moment
 * the discrepancy is real.
 *
 * 25km rather than something small because GPS is noisy in exactly the way that
 * matters here: a phone indoors, on a campus with buildings between it and the
 * nearest tower, can report a few hundred metres of drift between two readings
 * taken seconds apart. Rebuilding the whole deck for that would make the deck
 * visibly jump around, which is the exact problem the session model exists to
 * prevent. 25km is comfortably above the noise and well below any distance where
 * "near me" would be misleading.
 */
export const LOCATION_DRIFT_KM = 25;

/**
 * Coarse bands, nearest first. `maxKm: Infinity` is the catch-all tail so a
 * lookup always resolves rather than falling through to null.
 *
 * Labels are deliberately soft. The 300km+ band has `label: null` and renders
 * nothing — labelling thousands of distant strangers "Elsewhere in India" on
 * every card is noise, and the college badge already carries the useful part.
 */
export const DISTANCE_BANDS = [
  { maxKm: 30, label: 'Near you' },
  { maxKm: 100, label: 'In your area' },
  { maxKm: 300, label: 'Further away' },
  { maxKm: Infinity, label: null },
];

/**
 * Normalise an untrusted coordinate pair into a storable `[lat, lng]`, or null.
 *
 * Rounds to 2dp — this is the single privacy control for stored location and it
 * is deliberately the only way coordinates enter the database. Rejects out-of-
 * range values rather than clamping them: a latitude of 999 is corrupt data, and
 * clamping it to a plausible-looking 89 would launder a bug into something that
 * looks legitimate.
 *
 * @param {unknown} value
 * @returns {[number, number]|null}
 */
export const sanitizeLatLng = (value) => {
  if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length !== 2) return null;
  const [lat, lng] = value.map((n) => (typeof n === 'number' ? n : Number(n)));
  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lng)) return null;
  if (lat < -90 || lat > 90 || lng < -180 || lng > 180) return null;
  const round2 = (n) => Math.round(n * 100) / 100;
  return [round2(lat), round2(lng)];
};

/**
 * Great-circle distance in kilometres, or null when either point is unusable.
 *
 * Uses the haversine form rather than the law-of-cosines form specifically
 * because the latter loses catastrophic precision at small distances — the
 * distances that matter most here are 0–30km, where law-of-cosines can lose a
 * decimal place or more to floating-point cancellation.
 *
 * @param {[number, number]} a `[lat, lng]`
 * @param {[number, number]} b `[lat, lng]`
 * @returns {number|null}
 */
export const haversineKm = (a, b) => {
  const p1 = sanitizeLatLng(a);
  const p2 = sanitizeLatLng(b);
  if (!p1 || !p2) return null;

  const dLat = (p2[0] - p1[0]) * DEG_TO_RAD;
  const dLng = (p2[1] - p1[1]) * DEG_TO_RAD;
  const lat1 = p1[0] * DEG_TO_RAD;
  const lat2 = p2[0] * DEG_TO_RAD;

  const h =
    Math.sin(dLat / 2) ** 2 +
    Math.cos(lat1) * Math.cos(lat2) * Math.sin(dLng / 2) ** 2;

  return 2 * EARTH_RADIUS_KM * Math.asin(Math.min(1, Math.sqrt(h)));
};

/**
 * Resolve a distance to its band.
 *
 * @param {number|null} km
 * @returns {{index: number, label: string|null, maxKm: number}|null} null when
 *   `km` is unknown — callers MUST sort that last, not treat it as band 0.
 */
export const bandFor = (km) => {
  if (km === null || km === undefined || !Number.isFinite(km) || km < 0) return null;
  const index = DISTANCE_BANDS.findIndex((b) => km <= b.maxKm);
  if (index === -1) return null;
  return { index, label: DISTANCE_BANDS[index].label, maxKm: DISTANCE_BANDS[index].maxKm };
};

/**
 * Resolve a band INDEX back to its label.
 *
 * The deck sorts in Mongo by a bucket index rather than by a distance, because
 * sorting by a computed distance would put `null` first (nulls sort before
 * numbers in Mongo) and would also leak a precise distance across the sort
 * boundary. Only the index crosses back into JavaScript, so this is the inverse
 * of the ordering rather than a second way to compute a distance.
 *
 * @param {number} index
 * @returns {{index: number, label: string|null, maxKm: number}|null}
 */
export const bandFromIndex = (index) => {
  if (!Number.isInteger(index) || index < 0 || index >= DISTANCE_BANDS.length) return null;
  return { index, label: DISTANCE_BANDS[index].label, maxKm: DISTANCE_BANDS[index].maxKm };
};

/**
 * A user's location is usable for ranking only if it exists AND is fresh.
 *
 * @param {{currentLatLng?: number[], locationUpdatedAt?: Date|string}} user
 * @param {Date} [now]
 * @returns {boolean}
 */
export const isFreshLocation = (user, now = new Date()) => {
  if (!user) return false;
  if (!sanitizeLatLng(user.currentLatLng)) return false;
  if (!user.locationUpdatedAt) return false;
  const at = user.locationUpdatedAt instanceof Date
    ? user.locationUpdatedAt
    : new Date(user.locationUpdatedAt);
  if (Number.isNaN(at.getTime())) return false;
  const ageDays = (now.getTime() - at.getTime()) / 86_400_000;
  return ageDays <= LOCATION_TTL_DAYS;
};

/**
 * Convenience: the band between a viewer and a candidate, or null.
 *
 * The single call the deck needs, so the "unknown sorts last" rule is applied in
 * one place rather than at every call site.
 *
 * @returns {{index: number, label: string|null, maxKm: number}|null}
 */
export const bandBetween = (viewer, viewerPoint, candidatePoint, now = new Date()) => {
  if (!isFreshLocation(viewer, now)) return null;
  const km = haversineKm(viewerPoint, candidatePoint);
  return bandFor(km);
};

### ./server/utils/ladder.js

```
/**
 * 🪜 PROFILE LADDER — the single source of truth for profile completeness.
 *
 * This module OWNS the scoring. The client never computes a score: it renders
 * `User.profileScore`, which is written here and recomputed on every profile
 * write. That is deliberate — the ladder is used to GATE things (under 75 the
 * discover deck is read-only), so a client-computed score would be a number the
 * user can edit in devtools and walk straight through the gate with.
 *
 * The thresholds ship to the client via GET /config (`ladder`), so the gate and
 * the profile bar read the same marks instead of hardcoding their own.
 */

/** The three named rungs. Nothing else may invent a threshold. */
export const LADDER = {
  /** Visible to other people; discover deck is READ-ONLY below this. */
  publish: 45,
  /** Discover deck actions (flower / telegram / letter) unlock here. */
  interact: 75,
  /** Fully built profile. */
  aspirational: 100,
};

/** Mirrored by `slice(0, 4)` in routes/users.js and the client upload cap. */
export const MAX_PHOTOS = 4;
/** Mirrored by `prompts.slice(0, 3)` in routes/users.js. */
export const MAX_PROMPTS = 3;

/**
 * Point values per slot, in band order.
 *
 * ⚠️ THE GATE INVARIANT — read before changing any number here.
 *
 * The gate promises the user that ONE extra photo plus ONE prompt unlocks
 * their deck. That promise is only true if those two slots together equal
 * `interact - publish` (30). They currently do: photo2 (12) + prompt1 (18).
 *
 * If you re-weight photo2 or prompt1 so their sum is no longer 30, the gate
 * starts lying: the user adds a photo and a prompt exactly as told and stays
 * locked, with no way to work out why. There is no test that would catch this
 * from the UI — that is why the invariant is stated here and asserted in
 * scripts/backfill-ladder.mjs's companion assertions below.
 */
const WEIGHTS = {
  // ── 0 → 45 · publish ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  photo1: 15, // the face; on a dating card it is effectively the whole card
  gender: 10, // drives the mutual filter in discover.js, not just display
  name: 8,
  year: 6, // UG / PG
  intent: 6, // at least one entry
  // ── 45 → 75 · interact ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  photo2: 12,
  prompt1: 18, // ⚠️ see THE GATE INVARIANT above
  // ── 75 → 100 · aspirational ─────────────────────────────────────────
  photo3: 7,
  photo4: 4,
  prompt2: 9,
  prompt3: 5,
};

/**
 * Deliberately UNSCORED, do not add these without changing the bands above:
 *
 *   - `dob` / `age`  — an admission requirement (18+), not card content.
 *     /users/setup enforces it. Scoring it would make a safety gate look
 *     like a progress bar.
 *   - `bio`, `interests`, `pronouns`, `interestedIn` —
 *     real fields, but scoring them rewards filling them for points rather
 *     than because they make the profile worth replying to.
 *   - `college`, `collegeCode` — set by the auth picker, not by the user.
 *
 * Age is also DRIFT PRONE: `User.age` is written once at onboarding and goes
 * stale (see utils/age.js). Scoring a stale number would make the score wrong.
 */

/** A prompt earns its points only when it is actually answered. */
const isAnswered = (p) =>
  Boolean(p?.question?.trim()) && Boolean(p?.answer?.trim());

const hasText = (v) => typeof v === 'string' && v.trim().length > 0;

/**
 * Score a user document's CONTENT. Pure and synchronous: it touches no DB, no
 * Date.now(), and no ambient state, so it is trivially testable and safe to
 * call from any write path.
 *
 * Call this AFTER all field assignments and BEFORE `.save()`.
 *
 * @param {object} user a User document or a plain object with the same fields
 * @returns {number} 0–100
 */
export function computeScore(user) {
  if (!user) return 0;

  const photos = Array.isArray(user.photos) ? user.photos : [];
  const prompts = Array.isArray(user.prompts) ? user.prompts : [];
  const intent = Array.isArray(user.intent)
    ? user.intent
    : [user.intent].filter(Boolean);

  let score = 0;

  if (photos[0]) score += WEIGHTS.photo1;
  if (hasText(user.gender)) score += WEIGHTS.gender;
  if (hasText(user.name)) score += WEIGHTS.name;
  if (hasText(user.year)) score += WEIGHTS.year;
  if (intent.length > 0) score += WEIGHTS.intent;

  if (photos[1]) score += WEIGHTS.photo2;
  if (isAnswered(prompts[0])) score += WEIGHTS.prompt1;

  if (photos[2]) score += WEIGHTS.photo3;
  if (photos[3]) score += WEIGHTS.photo4;
  if (isAnswered(prompts[1])) score += WEIGHTS.prompt2;
  if (isAnswered(prompts[2])) score += WEIGHTS.prompt3;

  // Clamp rather than assert: if a future edit to WEIGHTS overflows, a 103
  // would break the client bar and the `>= 100` labels. Over-scoring is a bug
  // to fix, but it should degrade to "complete" rather than render nonsense.
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(LADDER.aspirational, score));
}

/**
 * Which band a score falls in. Single place the vocabulary is defined so the
 * client, the gate, and any future nudge copy all agree.
 *
 * @param {number} score
 * @returns {'locked'|'published'|'interactable'|'aspirational'}
 */
export function bandFor(score) {
  const n = Number.isFinite(score) ? score : 0;
  if (n >= LADDER.aspirational) return 'aspirational';
  if (n >= LADDER.interact) return 'interactable';
  if (n >= LADDER.publish) return 'published';
  return 'locked';
}

/** True when the deck's interactive actions should be available. */
export const canInteract = (score) => bandFor(score) === 'interactable' || bandFor(score) === 'aspirational';
```

const Header = ({ onNavigate, onSelectMatch, title, onSettingsToggle, visible = true }) => {
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const [drawerOpen, setDrawerOpen] = useState(false);
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  const { data: unreadData, refetch } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['unread-notifications-count'],
    queryFn: () => api.get('/notifications/unread-count'),
    refetchInterval: 30000,
  });
  const unreadCount = unreadData?.count || 0;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!drawerOpen) refetch();
  }, [drawerOpen, refetch]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleNewAlign = (_data) => {
      queryClient.setQueryData(['unread-notifications-count'], (old) => ({
        ...(old || {}),
        count: (old?.count || 0) + 1,
      }));
    };
    socket.on('new-align', handleNewAlign);
    return () => socket.off('new-align', handleNewAlign);
  }, [queryClient]);

  const toggleDrawer = () => {
    triggerHaptic('light');
    setDrawerOpen((prev) => !prev);
  };

  const handleLogoClick = () => {
    if (onNavigate) {
      triggerHaptic('light');
      onNavigate('discover');
    }
  };

  /* The feed tab, identified by the absence of a title. */
  const isDeck = !title || title === 'Deck';
  const showNotificationBell = isDeck;
  const showSettingsButton = title === 'Profile' && !!onSettingsToggle;

  /* badge — pops once per count change (remount via key), no infinite pulse */
  const bell = (
    <button className="hd-btn" onClick={toggleDrawer} aria-label="View notifications" title="Letters received">
      <Bell size={18} strokeWidth={2.6} />
      <AnimatePresence>
        {unreadCount > 0 && (
          <motion.span
            key={unreadCount}
            className="hd-badge"
            initial={reduceMotion ? false : { scale: 0 }}
            animate={{ scale: 1 }}
            exit={{ scale: 0, opacity: 0 }}
            transition={{ type: 'spring', damping: 12, stiffness: 300 }}
          >
            {unreadCount > 9 ? '9+' : unreadCount}
          </motion.span>
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </button>
  );

  /* wordmark — "matchalize", Caveat: white interior, black border. */
  const wordmark = (
    <div
      className="hd-wordmark"
      onClick={handleLogoClick}
      role={onNavigate ? 'button' : undefined}
      tabIndex={onNavigate ? 0 : undefined}
      onKeyDown={onNavigate ? (e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); handleLogoClick(); } } : undefined}
      title="matchalize — home"
    >
      <span className="hd-display hd-wm">matchalize</span>
    </div>
  );

  return (
    <>
      <style>{HEADER_CSS}</style>

      {/* One floating row on EVERY tab. On the Deck the center column is the
          wordmark with the scope chip under it. */}
      <motion.div
        data-deck-header
        animate={{ y: visible ? 0 : -110, opacity: visible ? 1 : 0 }}
        transition={reduceMotion ? { duration: 0 } : { type: 'spring', stiffness: 300, damping: 30 }}
        style={{ ...styles.bar, zIndex: 500, pointerEvents: 'none' }}
      >
        <div style={styles.slotLeft} />
        <div style={styles.slotCenter}>
          {isDeck ? (
            /* pointer-events auto re-enables the whole center column — the
               slot itself is pass-through, and this also guarantees the
               wordmark tap always lands. */
            <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', alignItems: 'center', gap: 3, pointerEvents: 'auto' }}>
              {wordmark}
            </div>
          ) : (title ? <span className="hd-display hd-heading">{title}</span> : null)}
        </div>
        <div style={styles.slotRight}>
          {showSettingsButton && (
            <button
              className="hd-btn"
              onClick={() => { triggerHaptic('light'); onSettingsToggle(); }}
              aria-label="Open settings"
              title="Settings"
            >
              <Settings size={18} strokeWidth={2.6} />
            </button>
          )}
          {showNotificationBell && bell}
        </div>
      </motion.div>

      {/* Notification Drawer */}
      <AnimatePresence>
        {drawerOpen && (
          <NotificationDrawer
            onClose={() => setDrawerOpen(false)}
            onSelectMatch={(match) => {
              setDrawerOpen(false);
              if (onSelectMatch) {
                onSelectMatch(match);
              } else if (onNavigate) {
                onNavigate('chat', { alignmentId: match._id });
              }
            }}
          />
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </>
  );
};

export default Header;
```

    <div className={`pc-ph-in${wide ? ' wide' : ''}`}>
      <img
        src={src || FALLBACK_IMG}
        alt=""
        draggable={false}
        loading="lazy"
        decoding="async"
        onLoad={(e) => e.currentTarget.classList.add('is-loaded')}
        onError={(e) => {
          const img = e.currentTarget;
          if (img.dataset.err) {
            img.classList.add('is-loaded');
            return;
          }
          img.dataset.err = '1';
          img.src = FALLBACK_IMG;
        }}
      />
    </div>
  </div>
);

const ProfileCard = ({
  profile = {},
  onAction,
  onSheetNearHeader,
  isGated = false,
}) => {
  const rootRef = useRef(null);
  const sheetRef = useRef(null);
  const menuBtnRef = useRef(null);
  const menuRef = useRef(null);
  const heroImgRef = useRef(null);
  const idRef = useRef(null);

  const setSheetRefs = useCallback((node) => {
    sheetRef.current = node;
  }, []);

  const profileIntent = useMemo(
    () => (Array.isArray(profile.intent) ? profile.intent : [profile.intent].filter(Boolean)),
    [profile],
  );

  const [rootH, setRootH] = useState(0);
  const [sheetH, setSheetH] = useState(0);
  const rootHRef = useRef(0);
  const sheetHRef = useRef(0);
  const entranceTimer = useRef(null);
  const entranceUntil = useRef(0);
  const entranceDoneFor = useRef(null);
  const peekHRef = useRef(0);

  const cancelEntrance = useCallback(() => {
    if (entranceTimer.current) {
      clearTimeout(entranceTimer.current);
      entranceTimer.current = null;
    }
    entranceUntil.current = 0;
  }, []);

  const computeBounds = (h, w) => {
    if (!h || !w) return { lo: 0, hi: 0, ready: false, short: true };

    const lo = Math.min(TOP_GAP, h - BOTTOM_GAP - w);
    const peek = peekHRef.current || PEEK_FALLBACK;
    const short = w <= peek;
    const hi = Math.max(lo, h - BOTTOM_GAP - (short ? w : peek));

    return { lo, hi, ready: true, short };
  };

  const boundsRef = useRef({ lo: 0, hi: 0, ready: false });
  boundsRef.current = computeBounds(rootH, sheetH);

  const yMV = useMotionValue(0);

  const photoScale = useTransform(yMV, (y) => {
    const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
    if (!ready || hi <= lo) return 1;
    const p = clamp((hi - y) / (hi - lo), 0, 1);
    return 1 + 0.06 * p;
  });

  const photoOpacity = useTransform(yMV, (y) => {
    const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
    if (!ready || hi <= lo) return 1;
    const p = clamp((hi - y) / (hi - lo), 0, 1);
    return 1 - 0.4 * p;
  });

  const entranceOpacity = useMotionValue(0);
  const entranceScale = useTransform(entranceOpacity, [0, 1], [0.92, 1]);

  const combinedPhotoOpacity = useTransform(
    [entranceOpacity, photoOpacity],
    ([entrance, drag]) => entrance * drag,
  );

  const combinedPhotoScale = useTransform(
    [entranceScale, photoScale],
    ([entrance, drag]) => entrance * drag,
  );

  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const SPRING = useRef(null);

  SPRING.current = reduceMotion
    ? {
        glide: { duration: 0 },
        bounce: { duration: 0 },
        wheel: { duration: 0 },
      }
    : {
        glide: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 170, damping: 30 },
        bounce: { type: 'spring', stiffness: 380, damping: 32 },
        wheel: { duration: 0.25, ease: 'easeOut' },
      };

  const glideControls = useRef(null);

  const stopGlide = () => {
    if (glideControls.current) {
      glideControls.current.stop();
      glideControls.current = null;
    }
  };

  const glideTo = (target, kind) => {
    stopGlide();
    glideControls.current = animate(
      yMV,
      target,
      SPRING.current[kind] || SPRING.current.glide,
    );
  };

  const [showMenu, setShowMenu] = useState(false);
  const [showReport, setShowReport] = useState(false);
  const [heroLoaded, setHeroLoaded] = useState(false);

  const showReportRef = useRef(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    showReportRef.current = showReport;
  }, [showReport]);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = rootRef.current;
    if (!el) return;

    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
      rootHRef.current = el.clientHeight;
      setRootH(el.clientHeight);
    });

    ro.observe(el);
    rootHRef.current = el.clientHeight;
    setRootH(el.clientHeight);

    return () => ro.disconnect();
  }, []);

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const el = sheetRef.current;
    if (!el) return;

    const measure = () => {
      const w = el.offsetHeight;
      sheetHRef.current = w;
      setSheetH(w);

      const idEl = idRef.current;
      if (idEl) {
        peekHRef.current = idEl.offsetTop + idEl.offsetHeight + PEEK_PAD;
      }

      const h = rootHRef.current;
      if (!h || !w) return;

      if (entranceDoneFor.current !== profile._id) {
        entranceDoneFor.current = profile._id;
        const rest = computeBounds(h, w).hi;
        cancelEntrance();
        entranceUntil.current = performance.now() + 900;
        yMV.set(h);

        entranceTimer.current = setTimeout(() => {
          entranceTimer.current = null;
          const hh = rootHRef.current;
          const ww = sheetHRef.current;
          const restNow = (hh && ww) ? computeBounds(hh, ww).hi : rest;
          entranceUntil.current = 0;
          glideTo(restNow, 'glide');
        }, 300);

        return;
      }

      if (performance.now() < entranceUntil.current) return;

      const { lo, hi } = computeBounds(h, w);
      const cur = yMV.get();
      const target = clamp(cur, lo, hi);

      if (Math.abs(target - cur) > 0.5) {
        stopGlide();
        yMV.set(target);
      }
    };

    measure();

    const ro = new ResizeObserver(measure);
    ro.observe(el);

    return () => {
      ro.disconnect();
      cancelEntrance();
      entranceDoneFor.current = null;
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    setShowMenu(false);
    setShowReport(false);
    setHeroLoaded(false);
    entranceOpacity.set(0);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [profile._id]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (reduceMotion) {
      entranceOpacity.set(1);
      return;
    }

    const controls = animate(entranceOpacity, 1, {
      duration: 0.5,
      ease: 'easeOut',
    });

    return () => controls.stop();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [reduceMotion]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (heroImgRef.current?.complete) setHeroLoaded(true);
  }, [profile.photos]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!showMenu) return;

    const onDown = (e) => {
      if (menuRef.current?.contains(e.target)) return;
      if (menuBtnRef.current?.contains(e.target)) return;
      setShowMenu(false);
    };

    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);

    return () => document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onDown);
  }, [showMenu]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!showMenu) return;

    const { lo, hi, ready, short } = boundsRef.current;
    if (!ready || short) return;

    const target = Math.max(lo, hi - MENU_RAISE);

    if (yMV.get() > target + 1) {
      stopGlide();
      glideTo(target, 'glide');
    }
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [showMenu]);

  const headerTriggerRef = useRef(null);
  const headerNearRef = useRef(false);
  const onSheetNearRef = useRef(onSheetNearHeader);

  useEffect(() => {
    onSheetNearRef.current = onSheetNearHeader;
  });

  const setHeaderNear = useCallback((near) => {
    if (headerNearRef.current === near) return;
    headerNearRef.current = near;
    onSheetNearRef.current?.(near);
  }, []);

  const measureHeaderTrigger = useCallback(() => {
    if (headerNearRef.current) return;

    const root = rootRef.current;
    if (!root) return;

    const bar = document.querySelector('[data-deck-header]');
    let headerBottom;

    if (bar) {
      headerBottom = bar.getBoundingClientRect().bottom;
    } else {
      console.warn(
        '[header-duck] [data-deck-header] not found — assuming 54px (DECK_TOP 12 + DECK_BTN 42)',
      );
      headerBottom = HEADER_FALLBACK_BOTTOM;
    }

    const rootTop = root.getBoundingClientRect().top;
    headerTriggerRef.current = headerBottom - rootTop - HEADER_LEAD;
  }, []);

  useMotionValueEvent(yMV, 'change', (y) => {
    const trigger = headerTriggerRef.current;
    if (trigger == null) return;

    if (headerNearRef.current) {
      if (y > trigger + HEADER_RELEASE) setHeaderNear(false);
    } else if (y < trigger) {
      setHeaderNear(true);
    }
  });

  useLayoutEffect(() => {
    const raf = requestAnimationFrame(() => {
      measureHeaderTrigger();
      setHeaderNear(false);
    });

    window.addEventListener('resize', measureHeaderTrigger);

    return () => {
      cancelAnimationFrame(raf);
      window.removeEventListener('resize', measureHeaderTrigger);
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => () => {
    headerNearRef.current = false;
    onSheetNearRef.current?.(false);
  }, []);

  const drag = useRef(null);
  const yBaseRef = useRef(0);
  const dragged = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const sheet = sheetRef.current;
    if (!sheet) return;

    const onDown = (e) => {
      if (showReportRef.current) return;
      if (e.pointerType === 'mouse' && e.button !== 0) return;
      if (drag.current) return;

      stopGlide();

      drag.current = {
        id: e.pointerId,
        startY: e.clientY,
        lastY: e.clientY,
        lastT: performance.now(),
        vel: 0,
        moved: 0,
      };

      yBaseRef.current = yMV.get();
      dragged.current = false;
    };

    const onMove = (e) => {
      const d = drag.current;
      if (!d || e.pointerId !== d.id) return;

      if (e.pointerType === 'mouse' && e.buttons === 0) {
        finish(e, false);
        return;
      }

      const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
      if (!ready) return;

      const dy = e.clientY - d.lastY;
      d.lastY = e.clientY;
      d.moved += Math.abs(dy);
      if (d.moved > 5) dragged.current = true;

      const now = performance.now();
      d.vel = d.vel * 0.7 + (dy / Math.max(1, now - d.lastT)) * 0.3;
      d.lastT = now;

      const raw = yBaseRef.current + (e.clientY - d.startY);

      if (raw < lo) {
        const over = lo - raw;
        yMV.set(lo - over * RUBBER);
      } else if (raw > hi) {
        const over = raw - hi;
        yMV.set(hi + over * RUBBER);
      } else {
        yMV.set(raw);
      }
    };

    const finish = (e, withMomentum) => {
      const d = drag.current;
      if (!d) return;
      if (e && e.pointerId !== undefined && e.pointerId !== d.id) return;

      const vel = withMomentum ? d.vel : 0;
      drag.current = null;

      const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
      if (!ready) return;

      const y = yMV.get();

      if (y < lo || y > hi) {
        glideTo(clamp(y, lo, hi), 'bounce');
        return;
      }

      const projected = clamp(y + vel * MOMENTUM_MS, lo, hi);
      if (Math.abs(projected - y) > 1) glideTo(projected, 'glide');
    };

    const onUp = (e) => finish(e, true);
    const onCancel = (e) => finish(e, false);

    sheet.addEventListener('pointerdown', onDown, true);
    window.addEventListener('pointermove', onMove, { passive: true });
    window.addEventListener('pointerup', onUp);
    window.addEventListener('pointercancel', onCancel);

    return () => {
      sheet.removeEventListener('pointerdown', onDown, true);
      window.removeEventListener('pointermove', onMove);
      window.removeEventListener('pointerup', onUp);
      window.removeEventListener('pointercancel', onCancel);
    };
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  const watchdogArmedRef = useRef(false);

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      watchdogArmedRef.current = true;
    }, 1500);

    return () => clearTimeout(timer);
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!watchdogArmedRef.current || drag.current) return;

    const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
    if (!ready) return;

    const cur = yMV.get();

    if (cur > hi + 1 || cur < lo - 1) {
      glideTo(clamp(cur, lo, hi), 'bounce');
    }
  });

  const onClickCapture = (e) => {
    if (dragged.current) {
      dragged.current = false;
      e.preventDefault();
      e.stopPropagation();
    }
  };

  useEffect(() => {
    const sheet = sheetRef.current;
    if (!sheet) return;

    const onWheel = (e) => {
      const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
      if (!ready) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      glideTo(clamp(yMV.get() - e.deltaY, lo, hi), 'wheel');
    };

    sheet.addEventListener('wheel', onWheel, { passive: false });

    return () => sheet.removeEventListener('wheel', onWheel);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, []);

  const onSheetKeyDown = (e) => {
    const { lo, hi, ready } = boundsRef.current;
    if (!ready) return;

    const step = 90;

    if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      e.preventDefault();
      glideTo(clamp(yMV.get() - step, lo, hi), 'glide');
    }

    if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      e.preventDefault();
      glideTo(clamp(yMV.get() + step, lo, hi), 'glide');
    }
  };

  const sheetReady = rootH > 0 && sheetH > 0;
  const prompts = profile.prompts || [];
  const interests = profile.interests || [];
  const photoB = profile.photos?.[1];
  const photoC = profile.photos?.[2];

  return (
    <div ref={rootRef} className="pc-root">
      <style>{PROFILE_CARD_CSS}</style>

      <motion.div
        className="pc-heroWrap"
        style={{
          scale: combinedPhotoScale,
          opacity: combinedPhotoOpacity,
        }}
      >
        <img
          ref={heroImgRef}
          src={profile.photos?.[0] || FALLBACK_IMG}
          alt={profile.name || 'Profile photo'}
          draggable={false}
          onLoad={() => setHeroLoaded(true)}
          onError={(e) => {
            const img = e.currentTarget;
            if (!img.dataset.err) {
              img.dataset.err = '1';
              img.src = FALLBACK_IMG;
            }
          }}
          decoding="async"
          className={`pc-hero${heroLoaded ? ' is-loaded' : ''}`}
        />
        <div className="pc-shade" aria-hidden="true" />
      </motion.div>

      <motion.div
        ref={setSheetRefs}
        className="pc-sheet"
        style={{ y: yMV, visibility: sheetReady ? 'visible' : 'hidden' }}
        onClickCapture={onClickCapture}
        onKeyDown={onSheetKeyDown}
        tabIndex={0}
        role="region"
        aria-label={`${profile.name || 'Profile'} details — drag or use arrow keys to move the card`}
      >
        <div className="pc-grabber" aria-hidden="true" />

        <div ref={idRef} className="pc-id">
          <div className="pc-idrow">
            <div style={{ minWidth: 0 }}>
              <h2 className="pc-name">
                {profile.name || 'Anonymous'}
                {profile.age ? <span className="pc-age">, {profile.age}</span> : null}
              </h2>
            </div>

            <button
              ref={menuBtnRef}
              type="button"
              className={`pc-iconbtn${showMenu ? ' pressed' : ''}`}
              aria-label="More options"
              aria-expanded={showMenu}
              onClick={(e) => {
                e.stopPropagation();
                setShowMenu((v) => !v);
              }}
            >
              <MoreVertical size={18} strokeWidth={2.5} />
            </button>
          </div>

          {profile.college && <p className="pc-college">{profile.college}</p>}

          {profile.distanceBand && (
            <p className="pc-college pc-distance">{profile.distanceBand}</p>
          )}

          {profile.gapYear && (
            <p
              className="pc-college"
              style={{
                fontWeight: 700,
                letterSpacing: '0.08em',
                textTransform: 'uppercase',
                fontSize: 11,
              }}
            >
              Gap year
            </p>
          )}

          <AnimatePresence>
            {showMenu && (
              <motion.div
                key="menurow"
                ref={menuRef}
                className="pc-menurow"
                initial={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                animate={{ height: 'auto', opacity: 1 }}
                exit={{ height: 0, opacity: 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: 0.16, ease: 'easeOut' }}
                style={{ marginTop: 16 }}
              >
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className="pc-menubtn"
                  onClick={() => {
                    triggerHaptic('light');
                    setShowMenu(false);
                    setShowReport(true);
                  }}
                >
                  <Flag size={14} strokeWidth={2.4} /> Report profile
                </button>
              </motion.div>
            )}
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>

        {profile.bio && (
          <div className="pc-sec">
            <SectionHead mark="green">About</SectionHead>
            <p className="pc-bio">{profile.bio}</p>
          </div>
        )}

        <div className="pc-sec">
          <SectionHead mark="coral">Vitals</SectionHead>
          <div className="pc-card" style={{ padding: 15 }}>
            <div className="pc-grid">
              <FieldCell
                icon={Calendar}
                color={TILE[1]}
                label="Year"
                value={profile.year || '—'}
              />
              <FieldCell
                icon={Sparkle}
                color={TILE[3]}
                label="Pronouns"
                value={profile.pronouns || '—'}
              />
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div className="pc-sec">
          <SectionHead mark="pink">Seeking</SectionHead>
          <div className="pc-pills">
            {(profileIntent.length ? profileIntent : ['Connection']).map((it, i) => (
              <span key={`${it}-${i}`} className="pc-chip acc">{it}</span>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>

        {interests.length > 0 && (
          <div className="pc-sec">
            <SectionHead mark="yellow" count={interests.length}>Interests</SectionHead>
            <div className="pc-pills">
              {interests.map((it, i) => (
                <span key={`${it}-${i}`} className="pc-chip">{it}</span>
              ))}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}

        {(prompts[0]?.question
          || prompts[1]?.question
          || prompts[2]?.question
          || photoB
          || photoC
          || profile.photos?.[3]) && (
          <div className="pc-sec">
            <SectionHead
              mark="coral"
              count={[
                prompts[0], prompts[1], prompts[2],
                photoB, photoC, profile.photos?.[3],
              ].filter(Boolean).length}
            >
              Exhibits
            </SectionHead>

            <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 16 }}>
              {prompts[0]?.question && (
                <PopoutItem
                  isGated={isGated}
                  targetId="prompt_0"
                  onAction={onAction}
                  style={{ display: 'block' }}
                >
                  <div className="pc-card pc-prompt">
                    <p className="pc-promptq">{prompts[0].question}</p>
                    {prompts[0].answer && (
                      <p className="pc-prompta">{prompts[0].answer}</p>
                    )}
                  </div>
                </PopoutItem>
              )}

              {(photoB || photoC) && (photoB && photoC ? (
                <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: '1fr 1fr', gap: 12 }}>
                  <PopoutItem
                    isGated={isGated}
                    targetId="photo_1"
                    onAction={onAction}
                    style={{ display: 'block' }}
                  >
                    <PhotoTile src={photoB} />
                  </PopoutItem>

                  <PopoutItem
                    isGated={isGated}
                    targetId="photo_2"
                    onAction={onAction}
                    style={{ display: 'block' }}
                  >
                    <PhotoTile src={photoC} />
                  </PopoutItem>
                </div>
              ) : (
                <PopoutItem
                  isGated={isGated}
                  targetId={photoB ? 'photo_1' : 'photo_2'}
                  onAction={onAction}
                  style={{ display: 'block' }}
                >
                  <PhotoTile src={photoB || photoC} wide />
                </PopoutItem>
              ))}

              {prompts[1]?.question && (
                <PopoutItem
                  isGated={isGated}
                  targetId="prompt_1"
                  onAction={onAction}
                  style={{ display: 'block' }}
                >
                  <div className="pc-card pc-prompt">
                    <p className="pc-promptq">{prompts[1].question}</p>
                    {prompts[1].answer && (
                      <p className="pc-prompta">{prompts[1].answer}</p>
                    )}
                  </div>
                </PopoutItem>
              )}

              {profile.photos?.[3] && (
                <PopoutItem
                  isGated={isGated}
                  targetId="photo_3"
                  onAction={onAction}
                  style={{ display: 'block' }}
                >
                  <PhotoTile src={profile.photos[3]} wide />
                </PopoutItem>
              )}

              {prompts[2]?.question && (
                <PopoutItem
                  isGated={isGated}
                  targetId="prompt_2"
                  onAction={onAction}
                  style={{ display: 'block' }}
                >
                  <div className="pc-card pc-prompt">
                    <p className="pc-promptq">{prompts[2].question}</p>
                    {prompts[2].answer && (
                      <p className="pc-prompta">{prompts[2].answer}</p>
                    )}
                  </div>
                </PopoutItem>
              )}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </motion.div>

      <AnimatePresence>
        {showReport && profile._id && (
          <ReportModal
            reportedUserId={profile._id}
            onClose={() => setShowReport(false)}
            onReported={() => {
              setShowReport(false);
              toast.success('Report submitted. Thank you for keeping the community safe.');
            }}
          />
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </div>
  );
};

export default ProfileCard;
