## 13. TEST-SETTINGS TABLE

**These are test settings. None is a commercial allowance or proven capacity.**

> **Roulette stays disabled until every required value is explicitly configured.**

| Setting | Env var | Test default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feature switch | `ROULETTE_ENABLED` | **`false`** | Must be explicitly `true` |
| Test account allowlist | `ROULETTE_TEST_ACCOUNTS` | **empty = nobody may queue** | Prevents a real account reaching a live queue |
| Max concurrent calls | `ROULETTE_MAX_CONCURRENT` | **5** | Founder-specified |
| Max queue size | `ROULETTE_MAX_QUEUE` | 25 | Bounds memory; overflow gets "busy" |
| Max wait | `ROULETTE_MAX_WAIT_SEC` | 300 | Then offer leave |
| Connection timeout | `ROULETTE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` | 20000 | |
| Pairing-offer validity | `ROULETTE_PAIR_TIMEOUT_MS` | 45000 | |
| Long-call policy | `ROULETTE_TEST_CALL_CEILING_MS` | **7200000 (2 h)** | **Runaway guard only**, deliberately far above any plausible product cap. A separate 30-min soak test proves no leak or stall |
| TURN credential TTL | `ROULETTE_TURN_TTL_SEC` | 3600 | Well under Cloudflare's 48 h max |
| Credential issuance | `ROULETTE_ICE_PER_HOUR` | 10 | Per user. Farm defence |
| Emergency disable | `ROULETTE_ENABLED=false` | — | Refuses new pairs, emits `call:terminated`, revokes TURN credentials |

### 13.1 Honest limits of the kill switch

- A **billing alert is not a spending cap.** Real protection is the concurrency cap +
  duration ceiling + admission control.
- **Stopping new pairings does not stop cost on existing calls.** Media already flowing
  continues until both sides stop.
- Revoking TURN credentials stops egress billing **immediately** — but the call dies.
- ⚠️ **A signaling command cannot guarantee termination of a modified client's direct media
  connection.** With P2P, the server cannot force a peer to stop sending. This is inherent
  to peer-to-peer media and must be described accurately, not papered over.

## 14. MODERATION

- Reports enter the existing review workflow.
- Preserve reporting context **without revealing profiles** to the other participant.
- **Review how the existing report-count escalation interacts with Roulette.**
  ⚠️ **[CONFIRMED] current behaviour: 3 reports → shadowban, 5 → suspension, with no human
  review** (`report.js:65-82`). **Do not introduce permanent sanctions solely from an
  unreviewed threshold without an approved policy.**
- ⚠️ **[CONFIRMED] the QA harness deliberately seeds one persona with `shadowbannedAt` and
  `contentFrozen: true`** (`seedSociety.mjs:169-172`) — automated shadowbans already appear
  in test data.
- **If safety controls fail, disable Roulette — not the controls.**

**No recording, face recognition, content uploads, or sampled-frame submission is
approved.** Neither is anything that resembles them by implication.

**Stage 1 scope clarification:** Stage 1 means *define the privacy contract, schema, and
tests first.* It does **not** mean finishing a sweeping rewrite of all UI components before
testing a camera preview. Privacy changes are implemented **incrementally, before the
relevant data can reach a partner** — see §6.

**Every stage:**
- Keep the feature behind a flag
- Use isolated testing data
- Report tests **actually run**
- Keep a rollback path
- **Do not silently alter Deck behaviour**
- **Do not proceed past a gate with failures outstanding**

**Must not regress:** profile discovery, matching, messaging, login, reporting, blocking.

## 16. ACCEPTANCE TESTS

### 16.1 Race tests

| ID | Setup | Action | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1** | A,B paired | Both send Align; both accept in the same tick | **Exactly 1** Alignment, **1** chat, **same** `alignmentId`; zero duplicate grants |
| **R2** | A sends Align | Call ends, then B accepts 1 s later | Rejected `EXPIRED`; **no** Alignment created |
| **R3** | A sends Align | B accepts and call closes simultaneously | Accept either commits before close (**survives**) or after (**expires**). Never both, never neither |
| **R4** | Not paired | A sends Align twice | One request row; second returns the same `notificationId` |
| **R5** | Hidden → revealed | Both send reveal simultaneously | Single `accepted` state; **exactly 2** grants, created once |
| **R6** | Reveal declined | Same person requests reveal again in the same connection | Rejected — no repeat pressure |

### 16.2 Queue tests

| ID | Setup | Action | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Q1** | A in queue | A double-taps Start | One queue entry, one session, one partner |
| **Q2** | A,B compatible | Match runs | Neither assigned twice |
| **Q3** | A blocked by B | Both wait | **Never paired** — checked at pair time, not just queue time |
| **Q4** | Small pool | Only recent partners available | Explicit "meet X again?" offered; **not** a silent hard block |
| **Q5** | No compatible partner | Wait | "Nobody compatible nearby right now" + 3 options; **no** automatic expansion |
| **Q6** | A skips B | B's session ends | "Conversation ended · Find next"; **no** new Align to A |
| **Q7** | A unmatches B | Both later in Roulette | **Never paired** |
| **Q8** | A,B already connected | Both in Roulette | Allowed; **no duplicate**, **no new Align**, "You're already connected · Open Chat"; existing grants preserved |

### 16.3 Privacy contract tests

| ID | Setup | Action | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Hidden A,B paired | Inspect every partner-facing payload | **Zero** occurrences of A's real `name`, `photos[]`, `college`, `email`, `dob` |
| **P2** | Hidden connection | A opens chat | Header shows **call name**; profile control **absent**, not merely disabled |
| **P3** | Hidden connection | A types | Remote receives **no** name in the typing event |
| **P4** | Hidden connection, B offline | Send message | Push **title and body** contain no real name |
| **P5** | Hidden connection | A types B's real name in Chats search | **No result** |
| **P6** | Hidden connection | Any profile-update save | `profile-updated` payload contains no real identity for a hidden partner |
| **P7** | Hidden request accepted | Inspect chat messages | **Zero** opening-letter rows; no copied photo/prompt text |
| **P8** | A visible, B hidden | Each views the other | A's profile reachable by B ✅; **A cannot** view B ✅ |
| **P9** | Mutual reveal accepted | Both open profiles | Real name + photos appear; **2** grants exist; row label stays the call name |
| **P10** | Screen-reader sweep | Hidden connection | No `alt` / `aria-label` contains the real name |
| **P11** | Blocked pair | Any payload path | Neither name reaches the other, **including** push |

### 16.4 Call-safety tests

| ID | Action | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Malformed / empty payload on every roulette socket event | Server survives; handler returns silently (pattern `chat.js:151-162`) |
| **C2** | Late ICE candidate from a prior `sessionId` | Rejected |
| **C3** | Socket dies without clean disconnect | Reaped within the reaper interval; partner re-queued with **original** wait start |
| **C4** | Refresh mid-call | Camera stops; partner returned to READY |
| **C5** | Network change mid-call | ICE restart; recover or cleanly end |
| **C6** | Report during call | Call ends immediately; reported user **never** re-paired |
| **C7** | Block during call | Call ends immediately; removed from any queue |
| **C8** | Open chat panel during call | **Call continues** — verified: Chat is a sibling (`AppShell.jsx:347` vs `:333`) |
| **C9** | Switch tab during call | "Leave this call?" → confirm ends, cancel preserves |
| **C10** | Back with panel open | Closes panel first, then offers to leave |

| Type | Covers | How |
|---|---|---|
| Unit / integration | R1–R6, Q1–Q8, P1, P7, P8 | `node:test` files in `server/tests/` |

| # | Question | Recommendation |

Does a Deck align grant access, overwriting hidden state? | **No silent upgrade.** Keep `source` immutable; require the hidden party to explicitly accept a "share profiles" request. Otherwise "Profile hidden" breaks by using the app normally |
| **2** | Should a Roulette Align permanently suppress that person's Deck card? | **Yes** — reuse the permanent-`archive` Interaction |

## 18. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE

- Group finder and double dates
- Missed-connections contact after a skip
- Payments and premium packages
- Automatic recording / content inspection / NSFW detection
- Full rebranding or internal-key renaming
- Multi-server architecture without demonstrated need
- Unlimited-use promises
- App-wide background calling
- Multiple independent request/chat systems
- Call-duration and daily-session **commercial** caps — deliberately undecided

**In scope** because the feature depends on them: authentication gaps, identity exposure,
request handling, and call safety.

## 19. WHAT MUST BE DISCLOSED IN THE UI

The honest full version of the privacy promise:

> "Roulette does not display your profile until you choose to share it — **within Roulette
> conversations.** If the same person appears in your Deck later, you will see their normal
> public profile. That is how Deck works."

**This must appear before the user chooses hidden mode**, not buried in a policy. It is the
single most likely source of the "I thought my profile was hidden" failure in §20.

**Also remove from the v1 placeholder screen** `[CONFIRMED]`:

Before a broader student launch, ask fresh testers to:

1. Start without revealing their profile
2. Explain what their partner can see
3. Send / accept Align
4. Find the saved conversation afterward
5. Share profiles mutually
6. Decline, leave, block, and report
7. Open and close chat without ending the call

**Watch especially for these — they are design failures to correct, not user mistakes:**

- "I thought Align revealed my profile."
- "I thought accepting meant agreeing to dating."
- "I couldn't find the request."
- "I accidentally left while opening chat."
- "I thought anonymous meant nobody could identify me."

One compact setup screen — **not** multiple compulsory onboarding pages.

Meet college students around your area.

So, what are you here for, huh?
[Social]  [Dating]  [Either]

Your call name
[Moonwalker                    Edit]

Profile hidden
Your face is visible. Your profile is not displayed.

[Preview & start]

Preferences
```

- Temporary names must **not** impersonate official staff or contain abusive content.
- Changing a name must **not** reset account restrictions, blocks, or report history.

by qwen:
The codebase is **exceptionally well-architected**. You have correctly implemented advanced, production-grade patterns such as atomic upserts to prevent race conditions, partial unique indexes, idempotency keys (`clientMsgId`), cursor-based pagination, and robust socket room management. 

However, after a deep scan of the provided dump, I found a few **Major Errors** and critical edge cases that could lead to security bypasses, 500 server crashes, or broken UX. 

Here are the major issues and how to fix them:

---

### 1. Critical Security: Admin "Kick" Doesn't Invalidate Session
**Location:** `server/routes/admin.js` & `client/src/utils/socket.js`
**The Bug:** When an admin forces a disconnect (`POST /api/admin/users/:id/disconnect`), the server emits a socket event, but **it does not invalidate the user's JWT**. 
If the client's socket disconnects or the user refreshes the page, the `matchalize_jwt` httpOnly cookie remains valid. Because `lastLogoutAt` was never updated, the `protect` middleware will happily authenticate them, effectively bypassing the admin's kick.

**The Fix:** 
Update `lastLogoutAt` in the admin route to instantly invalidate the JWT via your existing sliding expiration/multi-device check.
```javascript
// server/routes/admin.js
router.post('/users/:id/disconnect', async (req, res) => {
  if (!mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(req.params.id)) {
    return res.status(400).json({ message: 'Invalid user id' });
  }
  
  // 🛡️ INVALIDATE JWT SOCKET & COOKIE
  await User.findByIdAndUpdate(req.params.id, { lastLogoutAt: new Date() });

  const io = req.app.get('io');
  if (io) {
    io.to(req.params.id.toString()).emit('force-disconnect', {
      reason: 'Admin forced disconnect',
    });
  }
  res.json({ message: 'Disconnect signal sent' });
});
```
*(Note: On the client side, `socket.js` should also unconditionally clear `localStorage.removeItem('matchalize_user')` upon receiving `force-disconnect`, regardless of the reason).*

---

### 2. High Severity: Unhandled `CastError` (500 Crashes)
**Location:** `server/socket/chat.js`, `server/routes/messages.js`, `server/routes/matches.js`, `server/routes/report.js`
**The Bug:** Multiple routes and Socket events accept user-supplied IDs and pass them directly to Mongoose without validating them. If a malicious user or a buggy client sends an invalid string (e.g., `matchId = "abc"`), Mongoose throws a `CastError`, resulting in an unhandled **500 Internal Server Error** instead of a clean 400 Bad Request.

**The Fix:**
Add a quick validation middleware or inline checks.
```javascript
// Example for Socket Events (server/socket/chat.js)
socket.on('join-match', async (matchId) => {
  if (!matchId || !mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(matchId)) return;
  // ... rest of the code
});

socket.on('check-online', async ({ matchId, targetUserId }) => {
  if (!mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(matchId) || !mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(targetUserId)) return;
  // ...
});
```
*Apply `mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(req.params.id)` checks at the top of `GET/POST/DELETE /:matchId` and `/:id` routes in `messages.js`, `matches.js`, and `report.js`.*

---

### 3. Major UX Bug: Chat Search Jump Fails on Paginated History
**Location:** `client/src/pages/Chat.jsx`
**The Bug:** The `handleSearchJump` function attempts to scroll to a message using `document.querySelector(\`[data-msg-id="${msgId}"]\`)`. 
However, your chat uses **cursor-based pagination** (loading only the latest 50 messages). If a user searches for a keyword that exists in a message from 3 months ago, that message is **not in the DOM**. The `querySelector` returns `null`, and the jump silently fails, confusing the user.

**The Fix:**
You cannot rely on the DOM for search jumping in a paginated chat. When a search result is clicked, you must either:
1. Fetch the message's `createdAt` or `_id`, reset the chat's cursor to that point, reload the messages array, and *then* scroll.
2. Or, temporarily render a "Jump to original context" button that fetches the specific page of history containing that message.

---

### 4. Medium Severity: Fire-and-Forget Cloudinary Cleanup
**Location:** `server/routes/users.js` (Account Deletion)
**The Bug:** When a user deletes their account, you wipe their Cloudinary photos using a `forEach` loop:
```javascript
collectUserPhotos(user).forEach(url => deleteCloudinaryFile(url));
```
Because `deleteCloudinaryFile` is `async`, this is a "fire-and-forget" operation. If the Cloudinary API rate-limits or fails, orphaned media remains on your cloud storage indefinitely, and you have no retry mechanism or logging for the failures.

**The Fix:**
Use `Promise.allSettled` and log failures so a background cron job can clean them up later.
```javascript
const deletionResults = await Promise.allSettled(
  Array.from(collectUserPhotos(user)).map(url => deleteCloudinaryFile(url))
);
deletionResults.forEach((result, index) => {
  if (result.status === 'rejected') {
    console.error(`[Cleanup Failed] Orphaned media retained:`, result.reason);
    // TODO: Push to a cleanup queue/cron
  }
});
```

---

### 5. Edge Case: Brittle Image URL Validation
**Location:** `server/routes/users.js` (`isValidImageUrl`)
**The Bug:** The validation checks if the `pathname` ends with an image extension:
```javascript
return /\.(jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$/i.test(parsed.pathname);
```
If a user somehow submits an Unsplash URL with query parameters (e.g., `https://images.unsplash.com/photo-123?w=600&q=80`), `parsed.pathname` is `/photo-123`. The regex will fail, and the server will reject the profile setup with "One or more photo URLs are invalid." 
*(Note: Your frontend upload flow mitigates this by uploading to Cloudinary first, but if the frontend ever changes or a direct URL is passed, this will break).*

**The Fix:**
Check the extension against the full URL or ignore query parameters properly.
```javascript
const isValidImageUrl = (url) => {
  // ... existing trusted host checks ...
  // Extract extension before any query parameters
  const pathWithoutQuery = parsed.pathname.split('?')[0];
  return /\.(jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$/i.test(pathWithoutQuery);
};
```

---

### 6. Missing Rate Limiting on Destructive Actions
**Location:** `server/routes/messages.js` & `server/routes/report.js`
**The Bug:** You have excellent rate limiters for `discover` and `message sending`, but there is **no rate limiting** on:
*   `DELETE /api/messages/:matchId/:msgId` (Message deletion)
*   `POST /api/report/block/:userId` (Blocking)

A compromised client or malicious script could spam these endpoints, causing unnecessary DB write locks and Cloudinary API calls.

**The Fix:**
Add a lightweight limiter for destructive actions.
```javascript
// server/middleware/rateLimiters.js
export const destructiveActionLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 1 * 60 * 1000, // 1 minute
  max: 30, // 30 deletes/blocks per minute
  keyGenerator: (req) => req.user?._id?.toString() || req.ip,
  message: { message: 'Too many actions. Please slow down.' },
});

// Apply to routes:
router.delete('/:matchId/:msgId', protect, destructiveActionLimiter, async (req, res) => { ... });
router.post('/block/:userId', protect, destructiveActionLimiter, async (req, res) => { ... });
```

### Summary
Your implementation of the **Interaction Model** (using `archive`, `letter`, `seal_stamp` with cooldowns) and the **Discover Deck Engine** (using `randomSeed` for indexed range queries instead of `$sample`) is brilliant and highly optimized. 

Fixing the **Admin JWT invalidation** and the **Mongoose CastError** vulnerabilities should be your immediate priority before deploying to production.

glm5.3:
Nice, solid dump — I got through everything. Quick note before the list: **your paste cuts off mid-way through `models/Waitlist.js`** (inside `generateReferralCode`), and the `routes/`, `socket/`, and `utils/` files aren't in this share — a few findings below are marked "verify" because they depend on those.

---

## 🔴 Critical

**1. `dotenv.config()` runs *after* your imports (index.js)**
ESM imports are hoisted and executed before any module body code. `config/cloudinary.js` calls `cloudinary.config()` at module scope, so it runs **before** `.env` is loaded — `cloud_name`, `api_key`, `api_secret` are all `undefined`. It only works on Render because the platform injects real env vars; local dev with a `.env` file breaks silently.
```js
// first line of index.js, before all other imports:
import 'dotenv/config';
```

**2. `Block` model has no index on `blocked`**
`getBlockExclusionQuery` / `areBlocked` query `$or: [{ blocker }, { blocked }]`. The unique compound index `{blocker: 1, blocked: 1}` only serves the `blocker` branch — the `blocked` branch is a collection scan on every discover deck build.
```js
blockSchema.index({ blocked: 1 });
```

**3. `multer 1.4.5-lts.1` has known unpatched DoS vulnerabilities**
The 1.x line has multiple CVEs (malformed multipart request crashes). Upgrade to `^2.0.2`. Also, `multer-storage-cloudinary` is barely maintained — consider streaming straight to the Cloudinary SDK.

**4. OTPs stored in plaintext (models/OTP.js)**
A DB leak inside the 10-minute window exposes live, usable codes. Hash them (HMAC or bcrypt) and compare hashes on verify.

**5. Default-open environment posture (index.js)**
- `NODE_ENV === 'development'` → **all origins allowed with `credentials: true`**
- `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (i.e., unset or typo'd) → private LAN origins allowed

If `NODE_ENV` is ever mis-set on a deployment, you're silently permissive. Fail closed: hard-exit on missing `NODE_ENV`, or make the whitelist the only path in prod.

**6. Rate-limit drift + memory DoS surface**
`APP_CONSTANTS.API_RATE_LIMIT` says 100 req/15 min, but the actual limiter is **2000/min (~120k/hr)** combined with a 10MB body limit. That's ~20GB/min of parseable body per IP on a small dyno. Align the constant with the implementation — and actually use the constant instead of duplicating numbers.

---

## 🟠 Security / Design

- **`x-new-token` header undermines httpOnly** — the entire point of the httpOnly cookie is that XSS can't read the JWT, but the sliding-refresh path hands it to JS via a readable header. Since your SPA is same-origin, socket.io can read the cookie server-side in the handshake (`socket.handshake.headers.cookie`). Unless you have native mobile clients needing it, drop the header or move token rotation to a dedicated refresh endpoint.
- **socket.io CORS lacks `credentials: true`** — if frontend and API ever live on different domains, cookie auth silently fails on the polling transport.
- **CORS rejections return 500s** — `callback(new Error(...))` falls into your generic handler, so blocked origins get "The archival ledger encountered an unexpected tear." Use a proper 403, and honestly that 500 message will confuse *real* users hitting *real* errors too.
- **Malformed JSON → 500, not 400** — body-parser errors aren't `isOperational`. Add a branch for `err.type === 'entity.parse.failed'` / `'entity.too.large'`.
- **`uncaughtException` exits without flushing Sentry** — the exception never reaches Sentry. Use `Sentry.captureException(err)` → `await Sentry.close(2000)` → exit. Same applies to the SIGTERM path.
- **Graceful shutdown never closes Socket.IO** — `server.close()` won't fire its callback while websockets are open, so every deploy rides the 10s force-kill. Call `io.close()`.
- **`Report` unique `{reporter, reported}`** — a user can report someone **once, ever**. Second incident or escalating behavior → E1100. For a dating app this is backwards. Use a partial unique on *pending* reports or allow multiple.
- **Admin = single `ADMIN_EMAIL` env compare** — no role on the user, no audit trail, and anyone with env access silently becomes admin. Also duplicates token extraction from `auth.js`, and the `matchalize_jwt` cookie name is now hardcoded in **3 files**.
- **User model leak risk** — `adminNotes`, `suspendedReason`, `shadowbanScore`, `pushSubscription`, `randomSeed` live on the same doc served to users. Unless *every* route selects fields explicitly, these leak. Safer: strip in a `toJSON` transform or split admin data into another collection. *(Will verify in your routes file.)*
- **Per-email OTP limiter enables victim lockout** — anyone who knows a victim's `.ac.in` address can burn their 15-attempt bucket and block verification for 15 minutes.
- **`adminProtect` hands routes a `lean()` plain object** while `protect` gives a real Mongoose doc — `req.user.save()` in admin routes will crash. Inconsistent middleware contracts.
- **`/uploads` guard** — hardcoded cookie name, and verifies JWT but not `suspended`/`isDeleted`, so deleted users keep upload access until token expiry.

---

## 🟡 Performance / Reliability

- All rate limiters use the **in-memory store** — they reset on every deploy and don't share state across instances. Fine on one dyno; breaks the moment you scale to 2. Plan a Redis store.
- **Partial TTL index on Notification** — verify it actually built: Mongoose **silently logs** index-build failures, and partial TTL behavior is version-dependent. Check the Atlas index list.
- `deleteCloudinaryFile`'s transformation regex will also strip **real folders** that look like transformations (e.g., a folder named `f_images`), silently producing a wrong `public_id`.
- `Analytics` has no index on `user`/`event` and no TTL — funnel queries scan and the collection grows forever.

---

## 🔵 Minor / Cleanliness

- `Message.image` vs `mediaUrl` — two fields for the same job, drift guaranteed.
- `User`: stores both `age` and `dob` (they'll drift); `prompts.answer` has no maxlength; `ageRange` has no min ≤ max schema validation; `reactions` unbounded; `deleted: true` keeps full message text forever (privacy concern for a dating app).
- `Alignment`: nothing enforces exactly 2 users or `pairKey` ↔ `users` consistency.
- `Waitlist`: hardcoded defaults `IIT Bombay`/`iitb`; `referralCode` has both `unique: true` and `index: true` (redundant).
- `COLLEGE_MAP` has 10 IITs but your product description claims **all colleges of India** — one of these is wrong.
- helmet CSP keeps `localhost` in `connectSrc` even in production.
- Sentry: manually passing `expressIntegration()` **and** calling `setupExpressErrorHandler` is redundant (harmless — deduped — but noise).
- Express 5 landmines (fine today): `app.get('*')` and `express-mongo-sanitize@2.x` both break on Express 5.
- No tests, no linter, no CI.

---

## ✅ Genuinely good stuff

`pairKey` uniqueness, the partial unique index enforcing one opening letter per alignment, sparse `clientMsgId` dedup, ObjectId-cursor pagination, fail-fast env validation, the `lastLogoutAt` invalidation + sliding session combo, and the reasoning behind per-email OTP limiting (NAT'd campuses) is legitimately thoughtful.

---

Send the second file — I especially want to see `routes/upload.js` (does it re-config Cloudinary per request?), `routes/auth.js` (OTP verify logic, `.ac.in` enforcement), and how `/me`-style endpoints select User fields. 👀

## 🔴 Bug A — `sw.js` has a syntax error → the ENTIRE service worker fails to load

In the new `notificationclick` handler:

```js
self.clients.matchAll({ type: 'window', includeUncontrolled: true }).then((clients) => {   // ← not async
  ...
      await client.focus();   // ← await inside a non-async function = SyntaxError
```

`await` in a non-async callback is a **parse-time SyntaxError** — the whole `sw.js` file fails to evaluate, registration rejects, and the consequence chain is ugly:

- ❌ **Push notifications dead** (no SW = no push handler = no notification ever fires)
- ❌ Offline caching dead
- ❌ **The v2→v3 cache purge never runs** — the old caches full of users' voice notes and photos are *still sitting on devices*. The privacy purge everyone worked for is currently not happening, because the SW that would do the purging can't boot.

**Fix:**
```js
.then(async (clients) => {          // ← add async, that's it
```

**How to see it yourself:** DevTools → Application → Service Workers → red `SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions` — or just push a test notification and watch nothing happen.

## 🔴 Bug B — the warm-app message channel points at the wrong listener

`AppShell` entry point 2 listens on `window.addEventListener('message')` — but messages sent from a service worker via `client.postMessage()` arrive on the **`navigator.serviceWorker` container**, not `window`. As written: notification tapped while the app is open → tab focuses → chat never opens.

**Fix:**
```js
useEffect(() => {
  const onMessage = (event) => {
    if (event.origin !== window.location.origin) return;
    if (event.data?.type !== 'open-chat') return;
    openChatById(event.data.alignmentId);
  };
  // SW→page messages land here, NOT on window:
  navigator.serviceWorker?.addEventListener('message', onMessage);
  return () => navigator.serviceWorker?.removeEventListener('message', onMessage);
}, [matchData, queryClient]);
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Matchalize codebase dumper.

Emits paste-safe chunks under dumps/ instead of one multi-megabyte file.

WHY CHUNKED
-----------
A single ~1 MB paste is silently truncated by chat UIs long before any model's
context window is reached. The reader gets a plausible-looking prefix and
quietly misses the files that matter -- in practice the design-system files,
because alphabetical ordering buries them ~30% into the file. That failure mode
is worse than an obvious error: the model has no way to know it is missing half
the codebase, so it guesses and produces something that clashes with the real
design. Hence two hard rules below.

RULES ENFORCED
--------------
1. No chunk exceeds the byte budget (default 100 KB ~ 30k tokens). Files are
   never split mid-content; an oversize file gets its own chunk and is flagged.
2. Every discovered source file lands in exactly one chunk. Verified by
   re-parsing the written output and diffing each section against disk, then
   re-rendering and comparing bytes.

ORDER IS CURATED, NOT ALPHABETICAL
----------------------------------
The design-system files are emitted FIRST. They are the files that get lost,
and every other file is less useful without them.

OUTPUT
    dumps/00-INDEX.md      always safe to paste -- map, sizes, task recipes
    dumps/01-*.md ...      chunks, each within budget
    dumps/manifest.json    machine-readable inventory + verification result

    matchalize_full_dump.md   whole codebase in one file (NOT paste-safe)
    server_dump.md            server source only, one file (NOT paste-safe)

The two root monoliths are written on every run. They hold the same content as
dumps/ but without the paste budget, and they keep the historical filenames
working for anyone who referenced them. They are for local grep and for tools
without an attachment limit -- pasting them re-creates the truncation problem
described above. Share dumps/.

VERIFICATION
------------
Three independent checks run on every generate, and again under --check:
  1. Coverage: every discovered file appears in exactly one chunk.
  2. Content: each embedded section is diffed against the file on disk.
  3. Byte-exact: each output is re-rendered from its inputs and compared
     to what is on disk, so a stale header or trailing junk cannot pass.
--check also runs the monolith checks, so a stale monolith fails CI.

USAGE
    python3 regenerate_dumps.py                 # chunks + monoliths
    python3 regenerate_dumps.py --budget 60000  # tighter chunks
    python3 regenerate_dumps.py --check         # verify existing output only
    python3 regenerate_dumps.py --archive       # deprecated no-op
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DUMP_DIR = BASE_DIR / "dumps"

DEFAULT_BUDGET = 100 * 1024
# Code tokenizes closer to 3.5 chars/token than prose's ~4.
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.5

# Directories never worth dumping.

    "node_modules", ".git", ".vite", "dist", "build",
    ".nyc_output", ".scratch", "uploads", "__pycache__",
}
# Paths (relative fragments) excluded from the walk.
SKIP_PATH_FRAGMENTS = ("tests/qa/videos", "tests/qa/media", "tests/qa/report")
SKIP_NAMES = {".DS_Store", "package-lock.json", ".env", ".env.local", ".env.test"}

# Text types worth inlining verbatim.
SOURCE_EXTS = {
    ".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".mjs", ".cjs",
    ".css", ".svg", ".json", ".jsonc",
    ".html", ".md", ".yml", ".yaml", ".sh", ".py", ".txt", ".env.example",
}

# Root + build config, emitted verbatim.
CONFIG_FILES = [
    "package.json",

    ("server-core", lambda p: p.startswith("server/") and not (
        p.startswith("server/routes/") or p.startswith("server/tests/"))),
    ("server-routes", lambda p: p.startswith("server/routes/")),
    ("server-tests", lambda p: p.startswith("server/tests/")),
    ("docs", lambda p: p.endswith(".md")),
    ("tools", lambda p: p.startswith("scripts/") or p.endswith(".py")),
]

GROUP_BLURB = {
    "design-system": "Visual design language: tokens, theme components, fonts, "
                     "borders/shadows. Read this before writing any UI.",
    "shared": "Shared contracts: ladder thresholds, age/distance computation, college domain matching. Server owns logic; client mirrors constants for fallbacks.",
    "config": "Root and build configuration, CI, manifests.",
    "client-app": "Client entry point, root router, global stylesheet.",
    "client-assets": "Bundled images and SVG assets.",
    "client-utils": "Shared client helpers: API layer, haptics, hooks, deck chrome.",
    "client-components": "Shared React components.",
    "client-pages": "Screens / routes.",
    "server-core": "Server entry point, config, middleware, models, socket, utils.",
    "server-routes": "Express route handlers (API surface).",
    "server-tests": "Server test suites.",
    "docs": "Project documentation and handoffs.",
    "tools": "Build and automation scripts, including this generator.",
}

# Human recipes -> which groups you actually need to paste.
RECIPES = [
    ("Rebuild or restyle a screen",
     ["design-system", "client-pages", "client-components"]),
    ("Match the existing visual design",
     ["design-system"]),
    ("Edit the header / navigation",
     ["design-system", "client-components"]),
    ("Photo upload / media handling",
     ["client-utils", "server-routes"]),
    ("Auth, OTP, or account flows",
     ["client-pages", "server-routes", "server-core"]),
    ("Backend / API work",
     ["server-core", "server-routes"]),
    ("Debug a test failure",
     ["server-tests"]),
    ("Understand client-server contracts",
     ["shared", "design-system"]),
]

BINARY_MANIFEST_DIRS = ["client/public/icons"]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def human(n: int) -> str:
    if n >= 1024 * 1024:
        return f"{n / 1024 / 1024:.1f} MB"
    if n >= 1024:
        return f"{n / 1024:.0f} KB"
    return f"{n} B"


def est_tokens(text_or_bytes: int) -> int:
    return int(text_or_bytes / CHARS_PER_TOKEN)


def read(rel: str) -> str:
    return (BASE_DIR / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")


def fence_for(text: str) -> str:
    """Fence longer than the longest backtick run at any line start, so files
    containing ``` (markdown, shell) cannot break out of their block."""
    longest = 0
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        m = re.match(r"^`+", line)
        if m:
            longest = max(longest, len(m.group(0)))
    return "`" * max(3, longest + 1)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# discovery
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def walk(base: Path):
    if not base.is_dir():
        return
    for p in sorted(base.rglob("*")):
        if not p.is_file():
            continue
        rel = p.relative_to(BASE_DIR).as_posix()
        if any(part in SKIP_DIRS for part in p.relative_to(base).parts[:-1]):
            continue
        if any(frag in rel for frag in SKIP_PATH_FRAGMENTS):
            continue
        if p.name in SKIP_NAMES:
            continue
        if p.suffix.lower() not in SOURCE_EXTS:
            continue
        yield rel


def discover() -> list[str]:
    found: list[str] = []
    for rel in CONFIG_FILES + DOC_FILES + DESIGN_SYSTEM_FILES:
        if (BASE_DIR / rel).is_file():
            found.append(rel)
    for base in ["client/src", "client/public", "server"]:
        found.extend(walk(BASE_DIR / base))
    # de-dupe, preserve first-seen order
    seen, out = set(), []
    for rel in found:
        if rel not in seen:
            seen.add(rel)
            out.append(rel)
    return sorted(out)


def assign_groups(files: list[str]) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    pool = list(files)
    groups: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []

    for name, matcher in GROUP_ORDER:
        if name == "design-system":
            members = [f for f in pool if f in DESIGN_SYSTEM_FILES]
        elif name == "shared":
            members = [f for f in pool if f in SHARED_FILES]
        elif name == "config":
            members = [f for f in pool if f in CONFIG_FILES]
        else:
            members = [f for f in pool if matcher(f)]
        if members:
            chosen = set(members)
            pool = [f for f in pool if f not in chosen]
            groups.append((name, sorted(members)))

    if pool:
        # Never silently drop a file -- this is the invariant the whole
        # verification pass exists to protect.
        raise SystemExit(
            "ERROR: files matched no group (generator bug, would lose data):\n  "
            + "\n  ".join(pool)
        )
    return groups


def chunk_group(name: str, files: list[str], budget: int) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Roll files into chunks on file boundaries. Never splits a file."""
    sizes = {f: len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) for f in files}
    chunks: list[list[str]] = []
    current: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for f in files:
        size = sizes[f]
        # +2000 allows for this file's own heading/fence/wrapper overhead.
        if current and used + size + 2000 > budget:
            chunks.append(current)
            current, used = [], 0
        current.append(f)
        used += size
    if current:
        chunks.append(current)
    return chunks


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rendering
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def render_chunk(
    out: Path, title: str, group: str, files: list[str],
    idx: int, total: int, budget: int, stamp: str,
) -> dict:
    body_bytes = sum(len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) for f in files)
    oversize = [f for f in files if len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) > budget]

    out.write_text(render_chunk_text(title, group, files, idx, total, budget, stamp),
                   encoding="utf-8")

    return {
        "chunk": idx,
        "file": out.name,
        "group": group,
        "title": title,
        "files": files,
        "bytes": out.stat().st_size,
        "tokens": est_tokens(out.stat().st_size),
        "oversize": oversize,
    }


def render_chunk_text(title: str, group: str, files: list[str], idx: int,
                      total: int, budget: int, stamp: str) -> str:
    """Pure: same inputs always produce the same bytes. Verification re-runs
    this and compares, so it catches drift the section-level diff cannot see
    (a stale header, trailing junk, reordered files)."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    body_bytes = sum(len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) for f in files)
    oversize = [f for f in files if len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) > budget]

    header = [
        f"# Chunk {idx:02d} — {title}",
        "",
        f"> Matchalize · `{group}` · files {idx} of {total} chunks · "
        f"{len(files)} file(s) · {human(body_bytes)} · ~{est_tokens(body_bytes):,} tokens",
        f"> Generated {stamp}.",
    ]
    if oversize:
        header.append(
            "> WARNING: oversize file in this chunk "
            f"({', '.join(oversize)}). It could not be split; paste it on its own."
        )
    else:
        header.append(
            f"> Paste-safe: within the {human(budget)} / ~{est_tokens(budget):,} token target."
        )
    header.append(">")
    header.append("> Contains:")
    header.extend(f"> - `./{f}`" for f in files)
    header.append("")
    header.append("---")
    header.append("")
    parts.append("\n".join(header))
    for rel in files:
        text = read(rel)
        f = fence_for(text)
        parts.append(f"### ./{rel}\n\n{f}\n{text}\n{f}\n\n")
    return "".join(parts)


def render_monolith_text(title: str, sections, groups, stamp: str,
                         subtitle: str, with_binaries: bool = False) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """Pure, like render_chunk_text. Returns (text, files-in-order)."""
    gmap = dict(groups)
    parts = [
        "\n".join([
            f"# {title}",
            "",
            "> Verbatim contents of all project source and configuration files.",
            f"> Generated {stamp}.",
            f"> {subtitle}",
            f"> {NETWORK_SCOPE}",
            "",
            "> **This file is not paste-safe.** At this size a chat UI truncates the",
            "> paste silently and the reader cannot tell what it lost. To share this",
            "> codebase, paste `dumps/00-INDEX.md` and only the chunks you need.",
            "",
            "",
        ])
    ]
    emitted: list[str] = []
    for name, gnames in sections:
        members = [f for g in gnames for f in gmap.get(g, [])]
        if not members:
            continue
        parts.append(f"## Section — {name}\n\n")
        for rel in members:
            text = read(rel)
            f = fence_for(text)
            parts.append(f"### ./{rel}\n\n{f}\n{text}\n{f}\n\n")
        emitted.extend(members)
    if with_binaries:
        parts.append("\n".join(binary_manifest_lines(stamp)))
    return "".join(parts), emitted


def write_index(out: Path, chunks: list[dict], budget: int, stamp: str,
                verified: bool, total_files: int) -> None:
    by_group: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for c in chunks:
        by_group.setdefault(c["group"], []).append(c["file"])

    L = [
        "# Matchalize — Codebase Map",
        "",
        f"> Generated {stamp}. **This file is the one to paste first.**",
        "",
        "The codebase is ~1 MB of source, which no chat UI will accept in a single",
        "paste -- it gets truncated silently, and the model cannot tell you what it",
        "is missing. So it is split into chunks. Each is self-contained and within",
        f"the {human(budget)} / ~{est_tokens(budget):,} token paste target.",
        "",
        "## How to use this",
        "",
        "1. Paste this map.",
        "2. Paste only the chunks your task needs (see recipes below).",
        "3. If the model seems to be guessing about a file's contents, that file is",
        "   probably not in the chunks you sent -- ask for the specific chunk.",
        "",
        "## Chunks",
        "",
        "| Chunk | Group | KB | ~Tokens | Files | Contents |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for c in chunks:
        blurb = GROUP_BLURB.get(c["group"], "")
        L.append(
            f"| `{c['file']}` | {c['group']} | {c['bytes'] / 1024:.0f} | "
            f"~{c['tokens']:,} | {len(c['files'])} | {blurb} |"
        )

    L += [
        "",
        "## Task recipes",
        "",
        "Paste the listed chunks. Start with the design-system chunk unless the",
        "task is purely backend.",
        "",
    ]
    for label, groups in RECIPES:
        names: list[str] = []
        for g in groups:
            names.extend(by_group.get(g, []))
        if not names:
            continue
        L.append(f"- **{label}** — {', '.join(f'`{n}`' for n in names)}")

    L += [
        "",
        "## Verification",
        "",
        f"- Files covered: {total_files} (each in exactly one chunk)",
        f"- Chunks: {len(chunks)}, largest {human(max(c['bytes'] for c in chunks))}",
        f"- Round-trip re-parse: {'PASSED' if verified else 'FAILED'}",
        f"- Budget: {human(budget)}",
        "",
        "## Layout",
        "",
        "```",
        "client/src/utils/      shared helpers, API layer, design tokens",
        "client/src/components/  shared React components",
        "client/src/pages/      screens",
        "server/routes/         express API surface",
        "server/tests/          server test suites",
        "```",
        "",
    ]
    out.write_text("\n".join(L), encoding="utf-8")


def binary_manifest_lines(stamp: str) -> list[str]:
    L = [
        "## Section — Binary Assets",
        "",
        "> These files exist in the repo but are not inlined -- a binary in a",
        "> markdown code fence is unreadable garbage that just burns context.",
        "",
    ]
    for d in BINARY_MANIFEST_DIRS:
        base = BASE_DIR / d
        if not base.is_dir():
            continue
        rows = [p for p in sorted(base.rglob("*")) if p.is_file() and p.name != ".DS_Store"]
        if not rows:
            continue
        L += [f"### `{d}/`", "", "| File | Size |", "|---|---|"]
        for p in rows:
            L.append(f"| `{p.relative_to(BASE_DIR).as_posix()}` | {p.stat().st_size:,} bytes |")
        L.append("")
    return L


def write_binary_manifest(out: Path, stamp: str) -> None:
    out.write_text("\n".join(binary_manifest_lines(stamp)), encoding="utf-8")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# single-file monoliths
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Canonical network scope wording. ambitions/roulette.md references this
# sentence, so it must not drift.
NETWORK_SCOPE = (
    "Matchalize is an INTRA + INTER college network for all the colleges of "
    "India: users connect within their own campus (intra) AND across campuses "
    "(inter). Every user signs in via their own college academic email system "
    "(`.ac.in`), making each campus a private, verified community."
)

# group name -> which section it belongs to, in emission order.
# Client groups come before server so the design system leads, matching the
# chunk layout in dumps/.
MONOLITH_SECTIONS = [
    ("Root & Project Config", ["config"]),
    ("Shared Contracts", ["shared"]),
    ("Client Source", ["design-system", "client-app", "client-assets",
                       "client-utils", "client-components", "client-pages"]),
    ("Server Source", ["server-core", "server-routes", "server-tests"]),
    ("Docs & Meta", ["docs", "tools"]),
]

SERVER_SECTIONS = [("Server Source", ["server-core", "server-routes", "server-tests"])]

# Single source of truth for each monolith's identity. main() writes from this,
# verification re-renders from this -- so the two can never disagree.
MONOLITH_META = {
    "all": {
        "file": "matchalize_full_dump.md",
        "title": "Matchalize — Full Codebase Dump",
        "sections": MONOLITH_SECTIONS,
        "scope": "all",
        "with_binaries": True,
        "subtitle": (
            "Identical content to dumps/ -- kept as one file for grep and for "
            "tools without an attachment limit."
        ),
    },
    "server": {
        "file": "server_dump.md",
        "title": "Matchalize — Server Codebase Dump",
        "sections": SERVER_SECTIONS,
        "scope": "server",
        "with_binaries": False,
        "subtitle": (
            "Server source only. Excludes: .env, node_modules/, uploads/, "
            "dist/, build/, and package-lock.json."
        ),
    },
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# single-target bundles
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def resolve_target(needle: str, known: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """Accept a path, a basename, or a bare stem and pick the best match."""
    if needle in known:
        return needle
    cands = [r for r in known
             if Path(r).name == needle or Path(r).stem == needle
             or r.endswith("/" + needle)]
    if len(cands) == 1:
        return cands[0]
    if cands:  # ambiguous -- prefer a page, then the shortest path
        cands.sort(key=lambda r: (0 if "/pages/" in r else 1, len(r)))
        return cands[0]
    return None


def emit_sections(fh, files: list[str]) -> None:
    for rel in files:
        text = read(rel)
        f = fence_for(text)
        fh.write(f"### ./{rel}\n\n{f}\n{text}\n{f}\n\n")


def write_bundle(target: str, files: list[str], budget: int, stamp: str) -> Path:
    out = DUMP_DIR / f"bundle-{Path(target).stem}.md"
    total = sum(len(read(f).encode("utf-8")) for f in files)
    head = [
        f"# Bundle — {Path(target).stem}",
        "",
        f"> Generated {stamp}. **One file, one paste.**",
        f"> {human(total)} · ~{est_tokens(total):,} tokens · "
        f"{len(files)} file(s) · target {human(budget)}.",
        "",
        "You are working on:",
        f"**`./{target}`**",
        "",
        "Also included — the design system, because UI written without it clashes",
        "with the app's actual design language (tokens, fonts, borders, shadows):",
    ]
    head += [f"- `./{f}`" for f in files if f != target]
    head += ["", "---", ""]
    out.write_text("\n".join(head), encoding="utf-8")
    with out.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        emit_sections(fh, files)
    return out


def verify_bundle(out: Path, files: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    raw = out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    errors = []
    heads = list(re.finditer(r"^### (\./\S+)$", raw, re.M))
    if [h.group(1)[2:] for h in heads] != files:
        return [f"{out.name}: heading/file mismatch"]
    for h in heads:
        rel = h.group(1)[2:]
        fm = re.match(r"\n\n(`{3,})\n", raw[h.end():])
        if not fm:
            errors.append(f"{rel}: no fence")
            continue
        f = fm.group(1)
        start = h.end() + fm.end()
        end = raw.find("\n" + f + "\n", start)
        if end == -1:
            errors.append(f"{rel}: unterminated fence")
        elif raw[start:end] != read(rel):
            errors.append(f"{rel}: content differs from disk")
    return errors


def cmd_locate(needle: str) -> int:
    known = discover()
    target = resolve_target(needle, known)
    if target is None:
        print(f"ERROR: no file matches {needle!r}. Try a path, basename, or stem.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    mpath = DUMP_DIR / "manifest.json"
    if not mpath.is_file():
        print("ERROR: dumps/manifest.json missing — run: python3 regenerate_dumps.py",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    m = json.loads(mpath.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    hits = [c for c in m["chunks"] if target in c["files"]]
    print(f"{target}")
    if not hits:
        print("  (not in any chunk — binary or excluded)")
    for c in hits:
        print(f"  -> dumps/{c['file']}  ({human(c['bytes'])}, ~{c['tokens']:,} tokens)")
    ds = [c for c in m["chunks"] if c["group"] == "design-system"]
    if ds and target.startswith("client/src/") and not target.endswith(
            tuple(f for f in DESIGN_SYSTEM_FILES)):
        print("  plus the design system, if this is UI:")
        for c in ds:
            print(f"  -> dumps/{c['file']}  ({human(c['bytes'])}, ~{c['tokens']:,} tokens)")
    return 0


def cmd_for(needle: str, budget: int) -> int:
    known = discover()
    target = resolve_target(needle, known)
    if target is None:
        print(f"ERROR: no file matches {needle!r}. Try a path, basename, or stem.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    design = [d for d in DESIGN_SYSTEM_FILES if (BASE_DIR / d).is_file()]
    files = [target] + [d for d in design if d != target]
    # Trim design files if the bundle would blow the budget; never drop the target.
    while files and sum(len(read(f).encode()) for f in files) > budget \
            and len(files) > 1:
        files.pop()
    DUMP_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out = write_bundle(target, files, budget, datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"))
    errors = verify_bundle(out, files)
    size = out.stat().st_size
    if errors:
        print(f"FAILED verification ({len(errors)} problem(s)):", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errors:
            print(f"  {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if size > budget:
        print(f"NOTE: bundle is {human(size)}, over the {human(budget)} target — "
              f"`{Path(target).name}` is large. Send it alone.")
    print(f"Wrote {out.relative_to(BASE_DIR)}")
    print(f"  {human(size)} · ~{est_tokens(size):,} tokens · {len(files)} file(s)")
    print(f"  Paste this one file. Nothing else needed.")
    return 0



# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# verification
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def verify_sections_file(path: Path, expected: list[str], label: str) -> list[str]:
    """Re-parse a written dump and diff every embedded section against disk."""
    if not path.is_file():
        return [f"{label}: missing after write"]
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    errors: list[str] = []

    heads = list(re.finditer(r"^### (\./\S+)$", raw, re.M))
    listed = [h.group(1)[2:] for h in heads]
    if listed != expected:
        only_disk = sorted(set(expected) - set(listed))[:5]
        only_dump = sorted(set(listed) - set(expected))[:5]
        errors.append(
            f"{label}: file list mismatch "
            f"(expected {len(expected)}, found {len(listed)})"
            + (f"; missing {only_disk}" if only_disk else "")
            + (f"; unexpected {only_dump}" if only_dump else "")
        )
        return errors

    for h in heads:
        rel = h.group(1)[2:]
        fm = re.match(r"\n\n(`{3,})\n", raw[h.end():])
        if not fm:
            errors.append(f"{rel}: no opening fence")
            continue
        f = fm.group(1)
        # fm.end() is relative to the slice, so offset it by h.end().
        body_start = h.end() + fm.end()
        end = raw.find("\n" + f + "\n", body_start)
        if end == -1:
            errors.append(f"{rel}: unterminated fence")
            continue
        # Writer emits `text` verbatim and `end` sits on the newline the writer
        # added before the closing fence, so this must match read() exactly,
        # including any trailing newline.
        if raw[body_start:end] != read(rel):
            errors.append(f"{rel}: content differs from disk")
    return errors


def verify(chunks: list[dict], stamp: str) -> list[str]:
    """Verify the chunked dumps/ layout: every file exactly once, in budget,
    and each chunk byte-identical to a fresh render of its own inputs."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
    total = chunks[-1]["chunk"] if chunks else 0

    for c in chunks:
        p = DUMP_DIR / c["file"]
        errors += verify_sections_file(p, c["files"], c["file"])
        if p.is_file():
            want = render_chunk_text(c["title"], c["group"], c["files"],
                                     c["chunk"], total, c["budget"], stamp)
            if p.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != want:
                errors.append(f"{c['file']}: does not match a fresh render "
                              "(stale header, trailing content, or reordering)")
        for rel in c["files"]:
            if rel in seen:
                errors.append(f"{rel}: duplicated in {seen[rel]} and {c['file']}")
                continue
            seen[rel] = c["file"]

    expected = set(discover())
    missing = expected - set(seen)
    extra = set(seen) - expected
    if missing:
        errors.append(f"{len(missing)} file(s) never emitted: {sorted(missing)[:5]}")
    if extra:
        errors.append(f"unexpected file(s) emitted: {sorted(extra)[:5]}")

    for c in chunks:
        if c["bytes"] > c["budget"] and not c["oversize"]:
            errors.append(f"{c['file']}: {human(c['bytes'])} exceeds budget")
    return errors


def verify_monoliths(monoliths: list[dict], groups, stamp: str) -> list[str]:
    """Verify the single-file dumps: correct file set, correct content, and
    byte-identical to a fresh render."""
    errors: list[str] = []
    for m in monoliths:
        dest = BASE_DIR / m["file"]
        errors += verify_sections_file(dest, m["files"], f"monolith {m['file']}")
        if not dest.is_file():
            continue
        sections = MONOLITH_SECTIONS if m["scope"] == "all" else SERVER_SECTIONS
        want, emitted = render_monolith_text(
            MONOLITH_META[m["scope"]]["title"], sections, groups, stamp,
            MONOLITH_META[m["scope"]]["subtitle"],
            with_binaries=(m["scope"] == "all"))
        if dest.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != want:
            errors.append(f"monolith {m['file']}: does not match a fresh render "
                          "(stale header, trailing content, or reordering)")

        # The full dump must cover the entire codebase; the server dump must
        # cover exactly the server and nothing else.
        embedded = set(m["files"])
        if m.get("scope") == "all":
            expected = set(discover())
            if embedded != expected:
                only_disk = sorted(expected - embedded)[:5]
                only_dump = sorted(embedded - expected)[:5]
                errors.append(
                    f"monolith {m['file']}: not a full dump "
                    f"(missing {only_disk}, unexpected {only_dump})"
                )
        elif m.get("scope") == "server":
            stray = sorted(f for f in embedded if not f.startswith("server/"))
            if stray:
                errors.append(f"monolith {m['file']}: non-server files leaked in: {stray[:5]}")
    return errors


def check_existing() -> int:
    mpath = DUMP_DIR / "manifest.json"
    if not mpath.is_file():
        print("ERROR: dumps/manifest.json not found -- run: python3 regenerate_dumps.py",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    m = json.loads(mpath.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    budget = m["budget"]
    chunks = [dict(c, budget=budget) for c in m["chunks"]]
    errors = verify(chunks, m["generated"])
    # Monolith order derives from the current group assignment, so rebuild it
    # rather than trusting the recorded file list.
    groups = assign_groups(discover())
    errors += verify_monoliths(m.get("monoliths", []), groups, m["generated"])
    if errors:
        print(f"FAIL -- {len(errors)} problem(s):", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errors:
            print(f"  {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    monoliths = m.get("monoliths", [])
    print(f"OK -- {len(chunks)} chunks, {sum(len(c['files']) for c in chunks)} files, "
          f"largest {human(max(c['bytes'] for c in chunks))}, all round-trip clean.")
    for mo in monoliths:
        print(f"    {mo['file']:<28} {len(mo['files']):>3} file(s) {human(mo['bytes']):>8}")
    return 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--budget", type=int, default=DEFAULT_BUDGET,
                    help=f"max bytes per chunk (default {DEFAULT_BUDGET})")
    ap.add_argument("--archive", action="store_true",
                    help="(deprecated, no-op) monoliths are now always written")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
                    help="verify the existing dumps/ without regenerating")
    ap.add_argument("--locate", metavar="FILE",
                    help="print which chunk(s) contain FILE")
    ap.add_argument("--for", dest="target", metavar="FILE",
                    help="write a single minimal bundle for FILE (target + design system)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.archive:
        print("note: --archive is a no-op; the single-file monoliths "
              "(matchalize_full_dump.md, server_dump.md) are always written.",
              file=sys.stderr)

    if args.check:
        return check_existing()
    if args.locate:
        return cmd_locate(args.locate)
    if args.target:
        return cmd_for(args.target, args.budget)

    stamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    files = discover()
    groups = assign_groups(files)

    # Plan every chunk first so numbering is contiguous.
    plan: list[tuple[str, str, list[str]]] = []
    for gname, gfiles in groups:
        for part in chunk_group(gname, gfiles, args.budget):
            plan.append((gname, gname.replace("-", " ").title(), part))

    # Old output is removed wholesale so deleted source files cannot linger.
    if DUMP_DIR.exists():
        for old in DUMP_DIR.iterdir():
            if old.is_file():
                old.unlink()
    DUMP_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Index + manifest get number 00, so the first real chunk is 01.
    chunks: list[dict] = []
    for i, (gname, title, cfiles) in enumerate(plan, start=1):
        fname = f"{i:02d}-{gname}.md"
        meta = render_chunk(DUMP_DIR / fname, title, gname, cfiles,
                            i, len(plan), args.budget, stamp)
        meta["budget"] = args.budget
        chunks.append(meta)

    errors = verify(chunks, stamp)
    write_index(DUMP_DIR / "00-INDEX.md", chunks, args.budget, stamp,
                not errors, len(files))
    write_binary_manifest(DUMP_DIR / f"{len(plan) + 1:02d}-binaries.md", stamp)

    # Single-file monoliths are written on EVERY run. Same content as dumps/,
    # just unsectioned by paste budget — kept for local grep, for tooling with
    # no attachment limit, and because the old filenames are referenced.
    monoliths = []
    for scope in ("all", "server"):
        meta = MONOLITH_META[scope]
        text, emitted = render_monolith_text(
            meta["title"], meta["sections"], groups, stamp, meta["subtitle"],
            with_binaries=meta["with_binaries"])
        dest = BASE_DIR / meta["file"]
        dest.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        monoliths.append({
            "file": meta["file"],
            "scope": scope,
            "files": emitted,
            "bytes": dest.stat().st_size,
            "tokens": est_tokens(dest.stat().st_size),
        })

    # Verify monoliths BEFORE recording the manifest, so the manifest's
    # `verified` flag reflects all three surfaces rather than just the chunks.
    merrors = verify_monoliths(monoliths, groups, stamp)

    manifest = {
        "generated": stamp,
        "budget": args.budget,
        "chars_per_token": CHARS_PER_TOKEN,
        "file_count": len(files),
        "chunk_count": len(chunks),
        "total_bytes": sum(c["bytes"] for c in chunks),
        "max_chunk_bytes": max(c["bytes"] for c in chunks),
        "verified": not errors and not merrors,
        "errors": errors + merrors,
        "chunks": chunks,
        "monoliths": [
            {k: m[k] for k in ("file", "scope", "files", "bytes", "tokens")}
            for m in monoliths
        ],
    }
    (DUMP_DIR / "manifest.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"Wrote {len(chunks)} chunks + index + manifest to dumps/")
    print(f"  {len(files)} files, {human(manifest['total_bytes'])} total, "
          f"largest chunk {human(manifest['max_chunk_bytes'])} "
          f"(budget {human(args.budget)})")
    for c in chunks:
        flag = "  <- OVERSIZE" if c["oversize"] else ""
        print(f"    {c['file']:<34} {len(c['files']):>2} file(s) "
              f"{human(c['bytes']):>8}{flag}")
    print(f"Wrote {len(monoliths)} single-file monoliths (not paste-safe):")
    for m in monoliths:
        print(f"    {m['file']:<34} {len(m['files']):>3} file(s) {human(m['bytes']):>8}")
    if errors or merrors:
        n = len(errors) + len(merrors)
        print(f"\nFAILED verification ({n} problem(s)):", file=sys.stderr)
        for e in errors + merrors:
            print(f"  {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("\nVerification passed: every file round-trips byte-identically "
          "across all three surfaces.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

### ./scripts/generate-dump.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerates the Matchalize codebase dump.
#
# The pasteable output is CHUNKED into dumps/. A single ~1 MB paste gets
# silently truncated by chat UIs, and the reader has no way to tell what's
# missing -- so it loses the design-system files and then invents a UI that
# clashes with the real one.
#
# Two single-file monoliths are also written, for local grep and for tools
# without an attachment limit. Same content as dumps/, not paste-safe:
#   matchalize_full_dump.md   whole codebase
#   server_dump.md            server source only
#
# All logic lives in regenerate_dumps.py at the repo root; this wrapper exists
# so the old command still works.
#
#   dumps/00-INDEX.md   paste this first: map, sizes, task recipes
#   dumps/NN-*.md       chunks, each within the 100 KB paste target
#   dumps/manifest.json machine-readable inventory
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/generate-dump.sh                # default 100 KB chunks
#   bash scripts/generate-dump.sh --budget 60000 # tighter chunks
#   bash scripts/generate-dump.sh --check        # verify without regenerating
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
exec python3 regenerate_dumps.py "$@"
```

### ./scripts/generate-icons.mjs

```
import zlib from 'node:zlib';
import { writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'fs';
import { join } from 'path';

const BRAND = [249, 115, 22]; // #f97316
const WHITE = [255, 255, 255];
const BLACK = [0, 0, 0];

const crcTable = (() => {
  const t = new Uint32Array(256);
  for (let n = 0; n < 256; n++) {
    let c = n;
    for (let k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
    t[n] = c >>> 0;
  }
  return t;
})();

const crc32 = (buf) => {
  let c = 0xffffffff;
  for (const b of buf) c = crcTable[(c ^ b) & 0xff] ^ (c >>> 8);
  return (c ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
};

const chunk = (type, data) => {
  const len = Buffer.alloc(4);
  len.writeUInt32BE(data.length);
  const body = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(type, 'ascii'), data]);
  const crc = Buffer.alloc(4);
  crc.writeUInt32BE(crc32(body));
  return Buffer.concat([len, body, crc]);
};

const inHeart = (x, y) => {
  const a = x * x + y * y - 1;
  return a * a * a - x * x * y * y * y <= 0;
};

const buildPng = (size, mode) => {
  const raw = Buffer.alloc(size * (size * 4 + 1)); // 1 filter byte per row
  for (let y = 0; y < size; y++) {
    raw[y * (size * 4 + 1)] = 0; // filter: none
    for (let x = 0; x < size; x++) {
      const nx = (x / size) * 2.4 - 1.2;
      const ny = (y / size) * 2.4 - 1.2;
      const inside = inHeart(nx, ny * 0.9);
      const corner = Math.hypot(x - (size - 1) / 2, y - (size - 1) / 2) > (size / 2) * 0.92;
      const px = mode === 'icon' ? (inside ? WHITE : BRAND) : (inside ? BRAND : BLACK);
      const o = y * (size * 4 + 1) + 1 + x * 4;
      if (corner && mode !== 'badge') {
        raw[o] = raw[o + 1] = raw[o + 2] = 0;
        raw[o + 3] = 0;
      } else {
        raw[o] = px[0];
        raw[o + 1] = px[1];
        raw[o + 2] = px[2];
        raw[o + 3] = 255;
      }
    }
  }
  const ihdr = Buffer.alloc(13);
  ihdr.writeUInt32BE(size, 0);
  ihdr.writeUInt32BE(size, 4);
  ihdr[8] = 8; // bit depth
  ihdr[9] = 6; // color type: RGBA
  return Buffer.concat([
    Buffer.from([137, 80, 78, 71, 13, 10, 26, 10]),
    chunk('IHDR', ihdr),
    chunk('IDAT', zlib.deflateSync(raw)),
    chunk('IEND', Buffer.alloc(0)),
  ]);
};

const iconsDir = join(process.cwd(), 'client', 'public', 'icons');
mkdirSync(iconsDir, { recursive: true });

const specs = [
  { name: 'icon-192.png', size: 192, mode: 'icon' },
  { name: 'icon-512.png', size: 512, mode: 'icon' },
  { name: 'badge-72.png', size: 72, mode: 'badge' },
];

for (const { name, size, mode } of specs) {
  writeFileSync(join(iconsDir, name), buildPng(size, mode));
  console.log(`✓ Generated ${name} (${size}x${size})`);
}
```

### ./scripts/generate-server-dump.sh

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerates the server portion of the Matchalize dump.
#
# server_dump.md is written on every run and holds all server source in one
# file. It is ~340 KB, which is past the point where a chat UI truncates a
# paste, so it is for local grep only -- for sharing, use the `NN-server-*.md`
# chunks listed below.
#
# This wrapper regenerates everything (chunks and monoliths are produced
# together by one script) and then lists which chunks hold server code.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

python3 regenerate_dumps.py "$@"

printf '\nServer chunks — paste these for backend work:\n'
for f in dumps/*-server-*.md; do
  printf '  %-32s %s\n' "$f" "$(du -h "$f" | cut -f1 | tr -d ' ')"
done
```
